|     | $`\displaystyle\textup{With }\sigma_{x}`$ | $`\displaystyle:=\sum_{y\in[N]}\sigma_{xy}`$ |     | (B.5) |

and we parameterize $`F_{\theta}\in\mathbb{R}^{N\times k}`$ where
$`\forall x\in[N],F_{\theta}[x]=\sqrt{\sigma_{x}}h_{\theta}(x)^{\top}`$
for $`h_{\theta}:[N]\to\mathbb{R}^{k}`$, then
$`\mathcal{L}_{\textup{mf}}(F_{\theta})=\mathcal{L}_{\textup{mf}}(h_{\theta})`$
(overloading notation) is expressible in the following form.

|     |                                                             |                                                                                                                                                                            |     |                                          |
| --- | ----------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --- | ---------------------------------------- | --- | ----------- | --- | ----- |
|     | $`\displaystyle\mathcal{L}_{\textup{mf}}(h_{\theta})`$      | $`\displaystyle:=                                                                                                                                                          |     | \overline{A}-F*{\theta}F*{\theta}^{\top} |     | \_{F}^{2}`$ |     | (B.6) |
|     |                                                             | $`\displaystyle=\sum_{x,y\in[N]}\Big(\frac{\sigma_{xy}}{\sqrt{\sigma_{x}}\sqrt{\sigma_{y}}}-\sqrt{\sigma_{x}}\sqrt{\sigma_{y}}h_{\theta}(x)^{\top}h_{\theta}(y)\Big)^{2}`$ |     | (B.7)                                    |
|     |                                                             | $`\displaystyle=\textup{const}+\sum_{x,y\in[N]}\sigma_{x}\sigma_{y}(h_{\theta}(x)^{\top}h_{\theta}(y))^{2}-2\sum_{x,y\in[N]}\sigma_{xy}h_{\theta}(x)^{\top}h_{\theta}(y)`$ |     | (B.8)                                    |
|     |                                                             | $`\displaystyle=\textup{const}+\mathbb{E}_{x,x^{-}}(h_{\theta}(x)^{\top}h_{\theta}(x^{-}))^{2}-2\cdot\mathbb{E}_{x,x^{+}}h_{\theta}(x)^{\top}h_{\theta}(x^{+})`$           |     | (B.9)                                    |
|     |                                                             | $`\displaystyle=\textup{const}+\mathcal{L}_{\textup{cont}}(h_{\theta})`$                                                                                                   |     | (B.10)                                   |
|     | $`\displaystyle\textup{Where }\mathcal{L}_{\textup{cont}}`$ | $`\displaystyle:\mathcal{F}_{V}^{(k)}\to\mathbb{R}`$                                                                                                                       |     | (B.11)                                   |
|     | $`\displaystyle\mathcal{L}_{\textup{cont}}(h_{\theta})`$    | $`\displaystyle:=\mathbb{E}_{x,x^{-}}(h_{\theta}(x)^{\top}h_{\theta}(x^{-}))^{2}-2\cdot\mathbb{E}_{x,x^{+}}h_{\theta}(x)^{\top}h_{\theta}(x^{+})`$                         |     | (B.12)                                   |

Where $`\mathcal{F}_{V}^{(k)}`$ denotes the class of all functions
mapping $`V`$ to $`\mathbb{R}^{k}`$. Amazingly,
$`\mathcal{L}_{\textup{cont}}(h_{\theta}):=\mathbb{E}_{x,x^{-}}(h_{\theta}(x)^{\top}h_{\theta}(x^{-}))^{2}-2\cdot\mathbb{E}_{x,x^{+}}h_{\theta}(x)^{\top}h_{\theta}(x^{+})`$
is one version of the (population) contrastive loss function, similar to
what is used empirically.

[Equation B.8](#A2.E8 "In B.1.1 Setup ‣ B.1 Preliminary Lemmas ‣ Appendix B Theorems about Diffusion Similarity and Contrastive Learning ‣ A Theoretical Framework for Self-Play Theorem Proving Algorithms")
in the derivation above naturally defines the positive pair distribution
as where $`(x,y)\in[N]\times[N]`$ has marginal probability of
$`\sigma_{xy}`$ of being sampled. This corresponds to the sampling
process of first sampling an element from the base distribution first,
$`z\sim\mu`$, and then sampling the pair elements as independent
augmentations $`x\sim Q(z)`$, $`y\sim Q(z)`$, returning $`(x,y)`$.
Similarly, since a negative pair $`(x,y)\in[N]\times[N]`$ has marginal
probability of $`\sigma_{x}\sigma_{y}`$ in
[Equation B.8](#A2.E8 "In B.1.1 Setup ‣ B.1 Preliminary Lemmas ‣ Appendix B Theorems about Diffusion Similarity and Contrastive Learning ‣ A Theoretical Framework for Self-Play Theorem Proving Algorithms"),
the natural negative pair distribution corresponds to first sampling
$`z_{x},z_{y}\sim\mu`$ independently, and then sampling
$`x\sim Q(z_{x}),y\sim Q(z_{y})`$, returning $`(x,y)`$.

Crucially, since $`\mathcal{L}_{\textup{cont}}(h_{\theta})`$ and
$`\mathcal{L}_{\textup{mf}}(h_{\theta})`$ differ by only an additive
constant independent of $`h_{\theta}`$, we can understand the global
minimizers of $`\mathcal{L}_{\textup{cont}}`$ via the global minimizers
of $`\mathcal{L}_{\textup{mf}}`$. In particular, the Eckart-Young-Mirsky
Theorem characterizes the global minimizers of
$`\mathcal{L}_{\textup{mf}}`$ via the spectrum of $`\overline{A}`$
\[[13](#bib.bib39)\]. In the case $`\overline{A}=U\Sigma U^{\top}`$ is
p.s.d., then the global minimizer $`F_{k}\in\mathbb{R}^{N\times k}`$ is
of the form

|     |                                                |     |        |
| --- | ---------------------------------------------- | --- | ------ |
|     | $`\displaystyle F_{k}=U_{k}\Sigma_{k}^{1/2}R`$ |     | (B.13) |

Where $`R\in O^{k\times k}`$ is any $`(k\times k)`$ orthogonal matrix.

In addition to having an analytic characterization of the global minima,
one other useful property of $`\mathcal{L}_{\textup{cont}}`$ is that it
is written as an expectation, and so can be approximated by an empirical
risk. For a dataset $`\{\overline{x}_{i}\}_{i\in[n]}\subset V`$, define
the empirical contrastive loss as:

|                   |                                                                                                                                                                                 |                                                                                       |                       |        |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------- | ------ |
|                   |                                                                                                                                                                                 | $`\displaystyle\hat{\mathcal{L}}_{\textup{cont},n}(h_{\theta^{\prime}}):=`$           |                       | (B.14) |
|                   |                                                                                                                                                                                 | $`\displaystyle-\frac{2}{n}\sum*{i\in[n]}\mathbb{E}*{\begin{subarray}{c}x\sim Q(\cdot | \overline{x}\_{i}),\\ |
| x^{+}\sim Q(\cdot | \overline{x}_{i})\end{subarray}}(h_{\theta^{\prime}}(x)^{\top}h*{\theta^{\prime}}(x^{+}))+\frac{1}{n(n-1)}\sum*{i,j\in[n],i\neq j}\mathbb{E}\_{\begin{subarray}{c}x\sim Q(\cdot | \overline{x}\_{i}),\\                                                                 |
| x^{-}\sim Q(\cdot | \overline{x}_{j})\end{subarray}}(h_{\theta^{\prime}}(x)^{\top}h\_{\theta^{\prime}}(x^{-}))^{2}`$                                                                                |                                                                                       | (B.15)                |

Claim D.2 of \[[17](#bib.bib6)\] shows that
$`\mathbb{E}_{\{\overline{x}_{i}\}_{i\in[n]}\sim\mu}\hat{\mathcal{L}}_{\textup{cont},n}(h_{\theta})=\mathcal{L}_{\textup{cont}}(h_{\theta})`$,
i.e. that $`\hat{\mathcal{L}}_{\textup{cont},n}`$ is unbiased. Define
the empirical risk minimizer (ERM) as follows.

See
[3.2](#S3.Thmtheorem2 "Definition 3.2 (ERM, ϵ-minimizer). ‣ Contrastive Learning. ‣ 3 Preliminaries ‣ A Theoretical Framework for Self-Play Theorem Proving Algorithms")

[Algorithm 7](#alg7 "In B.1.1 Setup ‣ B.1 Preliminary Lemmas ‣ Appendix B Theorems about Diffusion Similarity and Contrastive Learning ‣ A Theoretical Framework for Self-Play Theorem Proving Algorithms")
describes a procedure to use empirical risk minimization to learn an
embedding model from finite samples from the base distribution.

1: i.i.d. sample access to base distribution $`D\in\Delta(V)`$,
augmentation function $`Q:V\to\Delta(V)`$, parameters
$`n,k\in\mathbb{N}`$, and embedding model class
$`\mathcal{F}_{\textup{emb}}`$ of models that embed into
$`\mathbb{R}^{k}`$

2: An embedding model $`h_{\theta}\in\mathcal{F}_{\textup{emb}}`$

3: Draw i.i.d. samples $`\bar{x}_{1},\ldots,\bar{x}_{n}\sim D`$

4: Define the empirical contrastive loss

|                                                                                                                           |                                                                               |                                                                                                          |     |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --- |
|                                                                                                                           | $`\displaystyle\hat{\mathcal{L}}_{\textup{cont},n}(h_{\theta^{\prime}}):={}`$ | $`\displaystyle-\frac{2}{n}\sum*{i\in[n]}\mathbb{E}*{\begin{subarray}{c}x\sim Q(\cdot\mid\bar{x}\_{i})\\ |
| x^{+}\sim Q(\cdot\mid\bar{x}_{i})\end{subarray}}\!\left[h_{\theta^{\prime}}(x)^{\top}h\_{\theta^{\prime}}(x^{+})\right]`$ |                                                                               |
|                                                                                                                           |                                                                               | $`\displaystyle+\frac{1}{n(n-1)}\sum\_{\begin{subarray}{c}i,j\in[n]\\                                    |

i\neq j\end{subarray}}\mathbb{E}_{\begin{subarray}{c}x\sim Q(\cdot\mid\bar{x}_{i})\\
x^{-}\sim Q(\cdot\mid\bar{x}_{j})\end{subarray}}\!\left[\left(h_{\theta^{\prime}}(x)^{\top}h\_{\theta^{\prime}}(x^{-})\right)^{2}\right].`$ | |

5: Compute
$`h_{\theta}\leftarrow\arg\min_{h_{\theta^{\prime}}\in\mathcal{F}_{\textup{emb}}}\hat{\mathcal{L}}_{\textup{cont},n}(h_{\theta^{\prime}})`$

6: return $`h_{\theta}`$

Algorithm 7 Learning Embeddings via ERM

As we will later see in
[Lemma B.1](#A2.Thmtheorem1 "Lemma B.1. ‣ B.1.2 Lemmas on Contrastive Learning ‣ B.1 Preliminary Lemmas ‣ Appendix B Theorems about Diffusion Similarity and Contrastive Learning ‣ A Theoretical Framework for Self-Play Theorem Proving Algorithms")
and
[Lemma B.2](#A2.Thmtheorem2 "Lemma B.2 (Generalization of ERM). ‣ B.1.2 Lemmas on Contrastive Learning ‣ B.1 Preliminary Lemmas ‣ Appendix B Theorems about Diffusion Similarity and Contrastive Learning ‣ A Theoretical Framework for Self-Play Theorem Proving Algorithms"),
under some assumptions, the empirical risk minimizer (ERM) will be also
approximately minimize the population contrastive loss. The assumptions
necessary for that result are expressed in terms of Rademacher
complexity, a core concept of Statistical Learning Theory. For
$`k\in\mathbb{N}`$, we use the definition of empirical Rademacher
complexity of a function class $`\mathcal{F}`$ of models
$`\mathcal{F}\ni h:V\to\mathbb{R}^{k}`$ used in \[[17](#bib.bib6)\].

See
[3.3](#S3.Thmtheorem3 "Definition 3.3 (Rademacher Complexity). ‣ Contrastive Learning. ‣ 3 Preliminaries ‣ A Theoretical Framework for Self-Play Theorem Proving Algorithms")

Note this definition takes a $`\max`$ over the $`n`$ datapoints
$`x_{1},\ldots,x_{n}`$ rather than an expectation, as is usual
\[[28](#bib.bib3)\].
[Lemma B.1](#A2.Thmtheorem1 "Lemma B.1. ‣ B.1.2 Lemmas on Contrastive Learning ‣ B.1 Preliminary Lemmas ‣ Appendix B Theorems about Diffusion Similarity and Contrastive Learning ‣ A Theoretical Framework for Self-Play Theorem Proving Algorithms")
analyzes the generalization error of the ERM, using Statistical Learning
Theory.

#### B.1.2 Lemmas on Contrastive Learning

###### Lemma B.1.

(Theorem 4.1 of \[[17](#bib.bib6)\]) Fix a base distribution
$`\mu\in\Delta(V)`$, augmentation function $`Q:V\to\Delta(V)`$, and
parameters $`k\in\mathbb{N}`$, $`k\leq|V|`$ and
$`p_{\textup{erm fails}}\in(0,1)`$. Let
$`\mathcal{F}_{\textup{emb}}\subset\mathcal{F}_{V}^{(k)}`$ be a class of
embedding models $`h_{\theta}`$ that map a domain $`V`$ into dimension
$`k`$ Euclidean space:
$`\mathcal{F}_{\textup{emb}}\ni h_{\theta}:V\to\mathbb{R}^{k}`$. Let
$`\mathcal{L}_{\textup{cont}}:\mathcal{F}_{V}^{(k)}\to\mathbb{R}`$ be
the population contrastive loss, instantiated with $`\mu`$ and $`Q`$, as
in
[Equation B.12](#A2.E12 "In B.1.1 Setup ‣ B.1 Preliminary Lemmas ‣ Appendix B Theorems about Diffusion Similarity and Contrastive Learning ‣ A Theoretical Framework for Self-Play Theorem Proving Algorithms"),
and
$`\hat{\mathcal{L}}_{\textup{cont},n}:\mathcal{F}_{V}^{(k)}\to\mathbb{R}`$
be the empirical contrastive loss over a i.i.d. dataset of size $`n`$
drawn from $`\mu`$, as in
[Equation B.15](#A2.E15 "In B.1.1 Setup ‣ B.1 Preliminary Lemmas ‣ Appendix B Theorems about Diffusion Similarity and Contrastive Learning ‣ A Theoretical Framework for Self-Play Theorem Proving Algorithms").
Assume:

1.  1.  For some $`\chi>0`$ that
        $`\forall h_{\theta}\in\mathcal{F}_{\textup{emb}},\forall x\in V`$,
        $`||h_{\theta}(x)||_{\infty}\leq\chi`$.
2.  2.  $`\mathcal{F}_{\textup{emb}}`$ contains at least one global
        minimizer of $`\mathcal{L}_{\textup{cont}}`$ over functions
        $`h:V\to\mathbb{R}^{k}`$

Then, with $`h_{\theta_{*}}\in\mathcal{F}_{\textup{emb}}`$ any global
minimizer of $`\mathcal{L}_{\textup{cont}}`$ and
$`h_{\hat{\theta}}\in\mathcal{F}_{\textup{emb}}`$ any global minimizer
of $`\hat{\mathcal{L}}_{\textup{cont},n}`$, for which a training dataset
of size $`n`$ was drawn i.i.d. from $`\mu`$, then with probability at
least $`1-p_{\textup{erm fails}}`$ over the randomness of the training
dataset,

|     |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |     |        |
| --- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --- | ------ |
|     | $`\displaystyle\mathcal{L}_{\textup{cont}}(h_{\hat{\theta}})\leq\mathcal{L}_{\textup{cont}}(h_{\theta_{*}})+\textup{poly}(k,\chi)\,\hat{\mathcal{R}}_{n/2}(\mathcal{F}_{\textup{emb}})+\textup{poly}(k,\chi)\,(\sqrt{\frac{\log\frac{2}{p_{\textup{erm fails}}}}{n}}+p_{\textup{erm fails}})`$ |     | (B.16) |

###### Proof.

Same as Theorem 4.1 of \[[17](#bib.bib6)\]. ∎

\[[17](#bib.bib6)\] say, as a comment immediately after their Theorem
4.1, that $`\hat{\mathcal{R}}_{n}(\mathcal{F})`$ typically looks like
$`\sqrt{\frac{\mathcal{C}(\mathcal{F})}{n}}`$ where
$`\mathcal{C}(\mathcal{F})`$ is an $`\mathcal{F}`$-dependent constant.
Assuming this is the case, then as a consequence of
[Lemma B.1](#A2.Thmtheorem1 "Lemma B.1. ‣ B.1.2 Lemmas on Contrastive Learning ‣ B.1 Preliminary Lemmas ‣ Appendix B Theorems about Diffusion Similarity and Contrastive Learning ‣ A Theoretical Framework for Self-Play Theorem Proving Algorithms"),
the minimizer of the empirical contrastive loss, with
$`n=\Theta(\frac{\mathcal{C}(\mathcal{F}_{\textup{emb}})\,\textup{poly}(k,\chi)}{\epsilon^{2}}\log\frac{1}{p_{\textup{erm fails}}})`$
i.i.d. samples, is $`\epsilon`$-minimizer embedding model with
probability at least $`1-p_{\textup{erm fails}}`$. We write this
explicitly in the following Lemma.

###### Lemma B.2 (Generalization of ERM).

Fix a base distribution $`\mu\in\Delta(V)`$, augmentation function
$`Q:V\to\Delta(V)`$, and parameters $`k\in\mathbb{N}`$, $`k\leq|V|`$,
and $`\epsilon\in(0,1)`$. Let
$`\mathcal{F}_{\textup{emb}}\subset\mathcal{F}_{V}^{(k)}`$ be a class of
embedding models $`h_{\theta}`$ that map a domain $`V`$ into dimension
$`k`$ Euclidean space:
$`\mathcal{F}_{\textup{emb}}\ni h_{\theta}:V\to\mathbb{R}^{k}`$. Let
$`\mathcal{L}_{\textup{cont}}:\mathcal{F}_{V}^{(k)}\to\mathbb{R}`$ be
the population contrastive loss, instantiated with $`\mu`$ and $`Q`$, as
in
[Equation B.12](#A2.E12 "In B.1.1 Setup ‣ B.1 Preliminary Lemmas ‣ Appendix B Theorems about Diffusion Similarity and Contrastive Learning ‣ A Theoretical Framework for Self-Play Theorem Proving Algorithms"),
and
$`\hat{\mathcal{L}}_{\textup{cont},n}:\mathcal{F}_{V}^{(k)}\to\mathbb{R}`$
be the empirical contrastive loss over a i.i.d. dataset of size $`n`$
drawn from $`\mu`$, as in
[Equation B.15](#A2.E15 "In B.1.1 Setup ‣ B.1 Preliminary Lemmas ‣ Appendix B Theorems about Diffusion Similarity and Contrastive Learning ‣ A Theoretical Framework for Self-Play Theorem Proving Algorithms").
Assume:

1.  1.  For some $`\chi>0`$ that
        $`\forall h_{\theta}\in\mathcal{F}_{\textup{emb}},\forall x\in V`$,
        $`||h_{\theta}(x)||_{\infty}\leq\chi`$.
2.  2.  $`\mathcal{F}_{\textup{emb}}`$ contains at least one global
        minimizer of $`\mathcal{L}_{\textup{cont}}`$ over functions
        $`h:V\to\mathbb{R}^{k}`$
3.  3.  $`\hat{\mathcal{R}}_{n}(\mathcal{F}_{\textup{emb}})\leq\sqrt{\frac{\mathcal{C}(\mathcal{F}_{\textup{emb}})}{n}}`$,
        where $`\mathcal{C}(\mathcal{F}_{\textup{emb}})`$ is an
        $`\mathcal{F}_{\textup{emb}}`$-dependent constant

Set $`p_{\textup{erm fails}}=\frac{\epsilon}{\textup{poly}(k,\chi)}`$.
Then, with $`h_{\theta_{*}}\in\mathcal{F}_{\textup{emb}}`$ any global
minimizer of $`\mathcal{L}_{\textup{cont}}`$ and
$`h_{\hat{\theta}}\in\mathcal{F}_{\textup{emb}}`$ any global minimizer
of $`\hat{\mathcal{L}}_{\textup{cont},n}`$, for which a training dataset
of size
$`n=\Theta(\frac{\mathcal{C}(\mathcal{F}_{\textup{emb}})\,\textup{poly}(k,\chi)}{\epsilon^{2}}\log\frac{1}{p_{\textup{erm fails}}})`$
was drawn i.i.d. from $`\mu`$, then with probability at least
$`1-p_{\textup{erm fails}}`$ over the randomness of the training
dataset,

|     |                                                                                                                        |     |        |
| --- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --- | ------ |
|     | $`\displaystyle\mathcal{L}_{\textup{cont}}(h_{\hat{\theta}})\leq\mathcal{L}_{\textup{cont}}(h_{\theta_{*}})+\epsilon`$ |     | (B.17) |

Equivalently, with $`F_{\hat{\theta}}\in\mathbb{R}^{|V|\times k}`$ where
$`\forall x\in[N],F_{\hat{\theta}}[x]=\sqrt{\sigma_{x}}h_{\hat{\theta}}(x)^{\top}`$
(with $`\sigma_{x}`$ defined in
[Equation B.5](#A2.E5 "In B.1.1 Setup ‣ B.1 Preliminary Lemmas ‣ Appendix B Theorems about Diffusion Similarity and Contrastive Learning ‣ A Theoretical Framework for Self-Play Theorem Proving Algorithms")),
then

|     |                                                              |     |                                                      |     |
| --- | ------------------------------------------------------------ | --- | ---------------------------------------------------- | --- | ----------- | --------------------------------------------------- | --- | ---------------------- | --- | -------------------- | --- | ------ |
|     | $`\displaystyle\mathcal{L}_{\textup{mf}}(F_{\hat{\theta}}):= |     | \overline{A}-F*{\hat{\theta}}F*{\hat{\theta}}^{\top} |     | ^{2}\_{F}`$ | $`\displaystyle\leq\min\_{F:\,\,\textup{rank}(F)=k} |     | \overline{A}-FF^{\top} |     | ^{2}\_{F}+\epsilon`$ |     | (B.18) |

###### Proof.

Apply
[Lemma B.1](#A2.Thmtheorem1 "Lemma B.1. ‣ B.1.2 Lemmas on Contrastive Learning ‣ B.1 Preliminary Lemmas ‣ Appendix B Theorems about Diffusion Similarity and Contrastive Learning ‣ A Theoretical Framework for Self-Play Theorem Proving Algorithms"),
plugging in
$`\hat{\mathcal{R}}_{n/2}\leq\sqrt{\frac{\mathcal{C}(\mathcal{F}_{\textup{emb}})}{n/2}}`$,
$`p_{\textup{erm fails}}=\frac{\epsilon}{\textup{poly}(k,\chi)}`$, and
$`n=\Theta(\frac{\mathcal{C}(\mathcal{F}_{\textup{emb}})\,\textup{poly}(k,\chi)}{\epsilon^{2}}\log\frac{1}{p_{\textup{erm fails}}})`$,
with the constant scaled so that the bound from
[Lemma B.1](#A2.Thmtheorem1 "Lemma B.1. ‣ B.1.2 Lemmas on Contrastive Learning ‣ B.1 Preliminary Lemmas ‣ Appendix B Theorems about Diffusion Similarity and Contrastive Learning ‣ A Theoretical Framework for Self-Play Theorem Proving Algorithms")
becomes

|     |                                                                |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |     |        |
| --- | -------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --- | ------ |
|     | $`\displaystyle\mathcal{L}_{\textup{cont}}(h_{\hat{\theta}})`$ | $`\displaystyle\leq\mathcal{L}_{\textup{cont}}(h_{\theta_{*}})+\textup{poly}(k,\chi)\,\hat{\mathcal{R}}_{n/2}(\mathcal{F}_{\textup{emb}})+\textup{poly}(k,\chi)\,(\sqrt{\frac{\log\frac{2}{p_{\textup{erm fails}}}}{n}}+p_{\textup{erm fails}})`$ |     | (B.19) |
|     |                                                                | $`\displaystyle\leq\mathcal{L}_{\textup{cont}}(h_{\theta_{*}})+\epsilon`$                                                                                                                                                                         |     | (B.20) |

This establishes
[Equation B.17](#A2.E17 "In Lemma B.2 (Generalization of ERM). ‣ B.1.2 Lemmas on Contrastive Learning ‣ B.1 Preliminary Lemmas ‣ Appendix B Theorems about Diffusion Similarity and Contrastive Learning ‣ A Theoretical Framework for Self-Play Theorem Proving Algorithms").
[Equation B.18](#A2.E18 "In Lemma B.2 (Generalization of ERM). ‣ B.1.2 Lemmas on Contrastive Learning ‣ B.1 Preliminary Lemmas ‣ Appendix B Theorems about Diffusion Similarity and Contrastive Learning ‣ A Theoretical Framework for Self-Play Theorem Proving Algorithms")
follows from
[Equation B.17](#A2.E17 "In Lemma B.2 (Generalization of ERM). ‣ B.1.2 Lemmas on Contrastive Learning ‣ B.1 Preliminary Lemmas ‣ Appendix B Theorems about Diffusion Similarity and Contrastive Learning ‣ A Theoretical Framework for Self-Play Theorem Proving Algorithms")
and
[Equation B.10](#A2.E10 "In B.1.1 Setup ‣ B.1 Preliminary Lemmas ‣ Appendix B Theorems about Diffusion Similarity and Contrastive Learning ‣ A Theoretical Framework for Self-Play Theorem Proving Algorithms"),
which we showed above:

|     |                                                                                                                                                  |     |        |
| --- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --- | ------ |
|     | $`\displaystyle\forall h_{\theta}\in\mathcal{F}_{\textup{emb}},\mathcal{L}_{\textup{mf}}(h_{\theta})=c+\mathcal{L}_{\textup{cont}}(h_{\theta})`$ |     | (B.21) |

Where constant $`c`$ is independent of $`h_{\theta}`$. ∎

Note that as the proof of
[Lemma B.1](#A2.Thmtheorem1 "Lemma B.1. ‣ B.1.2 Lemmas on Contrastive Learning ‣ B.1 Preliminary Lemmas ‣ Appendix B Theorems about Diffusion Similarity and Contrastive Learning ‣ A Theoretical Framework for Self-Play Theorem Proving Algorithms")
bounds the excess test loss of the ERM with uniform convergence, this
result can actually be strengthened: any
$`\frac{\epsilon}{2}`$-minimizer of the empirical contrastive loss, with
$`n=\Theta(\frac{\mathcal{C}(\mathcal{F}_{\textup{emb}})\,\textup{poly}(k,\chi)}{\epsilon^{2}}\log\frac{1}{p_{\textup{erm fails}}})`$
i.i.d. samples, is $`\epsilon`$-minimizer embedding model with
probability at least $`1-p_{\textup{erm fails}}`$.

#### B.1.3 The Connection Between Diffusion Embeddings and Contrastive Learning

In the following, assume the graph $`G=(V,E)`$ is finite
($`|V|<\infty`$), undirected, and connected.

###### Definition B.3.

(Spectral Diffusion Embedding) Let $`G=(V,E)`$ be a connected,
undirected graph. Let $`(V,P)`$ be a reversible Markov chain with
transition matrix $`P\in[0,1]^{|V|\times|V|}`$ and stationary measure
$`\pi`$. Define $`\{\phi_{i}\}_{i\in[|V|]}`$ as the right eigenvectors
of $`P`$ such that $`P\phi_{i}=\lambda_{i}\phi_{i}`$, with
$`1=\lambda_{1}\geq|\lambda_{2}|\geq\ldots\geq|\lambda_{|V|}|\geq 0`$.
The normalization of the eigenvectors is where $`\forall i\in[|V|]`$,
$`\textup{diag}(\pi)^{1/2}\phi_{i}`$ is a unit vector.³³ 3
Alternatively, note that since $`P`$ is reversible,
$`\textup{diag}(\pi)P`$ is symmetric. Let symmetric matrix
$`\overline{A}=\textup{diag}(\pi)^{1/2}P\textup{diag}(\pi)^{-1/2}=\sum_{i}\lambda_{i}v_{i}v_{i}^{\top}`$
with $`\{v_{i}\}_{i\in[|V|]}`$ being orthonormal. Then
$`\forall i\in[|V|],\,\phi_{i}=\textup{diag}(\pi)^{-1/2}v_{i}`$. Denote
$`\phi_{i}(x)`$ as the $`x`$-th entry of
$`\phi_{i}\in\mathbb{R}^{|V|}`$. For any $`t\in\mathbb{N}`$, define the
scale-$`t`$ spectral diffusion embedding as

|     |                                                                                 |     |                   |
| --- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --- | ----------------- | --- | --- | --- | ------ |
|     | $`\displaystyle\forall x\in V,\,\Phi*{t}(x)=(\lambda*{i}^{t}\phi*{i}(x))*{i\in[ | V   | ]}\in\mathbb{R}^{ | V   | }`$ |     | (B.22) |

Moreover, for any $`k\in[|V|],`$ define the $`k`$-truncated scale-$`t`$
spectral diffusion embedding as

|     |                                                                                                                |     |        |
| --- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --- | ------ |
|     | $`\displaystyle\forall x\in V,\,\Phi^{\leq k}_{t}(x)=(\lambda_{i}^{t}\phi_{i}(x))_{i\in[k]}\in\mathbb{R}^{k}`$ |     | (B.23) |

[Lemma B.4](#A2.Thmtheorem4 "Lemma B.4 (Diffusion Embeddings). ‣ B.1.3 The Connection Between Diffusion Embeddings and Contrastive Learning ‣ B.1 Preliminary Lemmas ‣ Appendix B Theorems about Diffusion Similarity and Contrastive Learning ‣ A Theoretical Framework for Self-Play Theorem Proving Algorithms")
establishes a connection between diffusion similarity and Euclidean
inner product of the spectral diffusion embeddings.

###### Lemma B.4 (Diffusion Embeddings).

Let $`G=(V,E)`$ be a connected, undirected graph. Let $`(V,P)`$ be a
reversible Markov chain with transition matrix
$`P\in[0,1]^{|V|\times|V|}`$ and stationary measure $`\pi`$. For any
$`t\in\mathbb{N}`$ and $`x\in V`$, with
$`\Phi_{t}(x)=(\lambda_{i}^{t}\phi_{i}(x))_{i\in[|V|]}\in\mathbb{R}^{|V|}`$
denoting the spectral diffusion embedding of $`x`$ as in
[Definition B.3](#A2.Thmtheorem3 "Definition B.3. ‣ B.1.3 The Connection Between Diffusion Embeddings and Contrastive Learning ‣ B.1 Preliminary Lemmas ‣ Appendix B Theorems about Diffusion Similarity and Contrastive Learning ‣ A Theoretical Framework for Self-Play Theorem Proving Algorithms"),
we have

|     |                                                                                                                            |     |        |
| --- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --- | ------ |
|     | $`\displaystyle\forall x,y\in V,\langle\Phi_{t}(x),\Phi_{t}(y)\rangle=\langle p^{t}(x),p^{t}(y)\rangle_{\ell^{2}(1/\pi)}`$ |     | (B.24) |

where $`\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle`$ is the usual Euclidean inner product
and $`\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_{\ell^{2}(1/\pi)}`$ is the inner product
where $`\forall i\in[|V|]`$, the $`i`$th term is weighted by
$`\frac{1}{\pi(i)}`$.

###### Proof.

Because $`(V,P)`$ is reversible, let
$`P=D^{-1}W\in\mathbb{R}^{|V|\times|V|}`$ where
$`D=\textup{diag}(W\mathbf{1})=\textup{diag}(\pi)`$ and
$`W=\textup{diag}(\pi)P\in\mathbb{R}^{|V|\times|V|}`$ is symmetric. The
symmetric matrix $`\overline{A}=D^{-1/2}WD^{-1/2}`$ is the normalized
adjacency matrix, with eigendecomposition
$`\overline{A}=\sum_{i\in[|V|]}\lambda_{i}u_{i}u_{i}^{\top}`$. Since
$`P=D^{-1/2}\overline{A}D^{1/2}`$, then
$`P=\sum_{i\in[|V|]}\lambda_{i}(D^{-1/2}u_{i})(D^{1/2}u_{i})^{\top}`$,
so that $`\forall i\in[|V|],\phi_{i}=D^{-1/2}u_{i}`$. Now, for any
$`t\in\mathbb{N}`$ and $`x\in V`$,

|     |                            |                                                        |     |                                      |
| --- | -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ | --- | ------------------------------------ | --- | ------ |
|     | $`\displaystyle p^{t}(x)`$ | $`\displaystyle:=(P^{\top})^{t}e_{x}`$                 |     | (B.25)                               |
|     |                            | $`\displaystyle=D^{1/2}\overline{A}^{t}D^{-1/2}e_{x}`$ |     | (B.26)                               |
|     |                            | $`\displaystyle=D^{1/2}\sum\_{i\in[                    | V   | ]}\lambda*{i}^{t}u*{i}\phi\_{i}(x)`$ |     | (B.27) |
|     |                            | $`\displaystyle=D^{1/2}U\Phi_{t}(x)`$                  |     | (B.28)                               |

Where $`U`$ is an orthogonal transformation
$`U=[u_{1},\ldots,u_{|V|}]\in\mathbb{R}^{|V|\times|V|}`$. It follows
that for any $`x,y\in V`$,

|     |                                                                     |                                                          |     |        |
| --- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- | --- | ------ |
|     | $`\displaystyle\langle p^{t}(x),p^{t}(y)\rangle_{\ell^{2}(1/\pi)}`$ | $`\displaystyle:=(p^{t}(x))^{\top}D^{-1}p^{t}(y)`$       |     | (B.29) |
|     |                                                                     | $`\displaystyle=\Phi_{t}(x)^{\top}U^{\top}U\Phi_{t}(y)`$ |     | (B.30) |
|     |                                                                     | $`\displaystyle=\Phi_{t}(x)^{\top}\Phi_{t}(y)`$          |     | (B.31) |

∎

As a corollary, for any $`u,v\in V`$, the diffusion distance
$`||p^{t}(u)-p^{t}(v)||_{\ell^{2}(1/\pi)}=||\Phi_{t}(u)-\Phi_{t}(v)||_{2}`$.
For more about diffusion distance, see \[[10](#bib.bib36)\] and
\[[43](#bib.bib8)\].

The following Lemma describes the approximation properties of a
diffusion embedding with small embedding dimension $`k\in[|V|-1]`$
(rather than the full $`|V|`$-dimensional embedding), when
$`\lambda_{k+1}^{2t}`$ is small.

###### Lemma B.5.

(Small Embedding Dimension Approximation; Lemma 2 of
\[[43](#bib.bib8)\]) Let $`G=(V,E)`$ be a connected, undirected graph.
Let $`(V,P)`$ be a reversible Markov chain with transition matrix
$`P\in[0,1]^{|V|\times|V|}`$ and stationary measure $`\pi`$. Let
$`\pi_{\textup{min}}:=\min_{v\in V}\pi(v)`$ and
$`1=\lambda_{1}\geq|\lambda_{2}|\geq\ldots,\geq|\lambda_{|V|}|\geq 0`$
be arranged in decreasing magnitude. Given $`t\in\mathbb{N}`$ and
$`k\in[|V|-1]`$, for any $`u,v\in V`$,

|     |                                                                                                      |                                                                                                                                                                     |                         |        |
| --- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------- | ------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------- | --- | ----------------------------------------- | --- | ------------- | --- | ----------------------- | --- | ----------- | --- | ------ |
|     | $`\displaystyle                                                                                      |                                                                                                                                                                     | \Phi*{t}(u)-\Phi*{t}(v) |        | _{2}^{2}-\frac{2\lambda_{k+1}^{2t}}{\pi\_{\textup{min}}}\cdot 1[u\neq v]`$ | $`\displaystyle\leq |     | \Phi^{\leq k}_{t}(u)-\Phi^{\leq k}_{t}(v) |     | \_{2}^{2}\leq |     | \Phi*{t}(u)-\Phi*{t}(v) |     | \_{2}^{2}`$ |     | (B.32) |
|     | $`\displaystyle                                                                                      |                                                                                                                                                                     | \Phi\_{t}(v)            |        | _{2}^{2}-\frac{\lambda_{k+1}^{2t}}{\pi\_{\textup{min}}}`$                  | $`\displaystyle\leq |     | \Phi\_{t}^{\leq k}(v)                     |     | \_{2}^{2}\leq |     | \Phi\_{t}(v)            |     | \_{2}^{2}`$ |     | (B.33) |
|     | $`\displaystyle\langle\Phi_{t}(u),\Phi_{t}(v)\rangle-\frac{\lambda_{k+1}^{2t}}{\pi_{\textup{min}}}`$ | $`\displaystyle\leq\langle\Phi_{t}^{\leq k}(u),\Phi_{t}^{\leq k}(v)\rangle\leq\langle\Phi_{t}(u),\Phi_{t}(v)\rangle+\frac{\lambda_{k+1}^{2t}}{\pi_{\textup{min}}}`$ |                         | (B.34) |

###### Proof.

As in the proof of
[Lemma B.6](#A2.Thmtheorem6 "Lemma B.6 (Global Minimizers for Contrastive Loss). ‣ B.1.3 The Connection Between Diffusion Embeddings and Contrastive Learning ‣ B.1 Preliminary Lemmas ‣ Appendix B Theorems about Diffusion Similarity and Contrastive Learning ‣ A Theoretical Framework for Self-Play Theorem Proving Algorithms"),
with $`D=\textup{diag}(\pi)`$ and matrix $`D^{1/2}PD^{-1/2}`$ having
eigendecomposition $`U\Lambda U^{\top}`$, then
$`P=(D^{-1/2}U)\Lambda(D^{1/2}U)^{\top}`$.

The matrix of right eigenvectors
$`\Phi:=[\phi_{1},\ldots,\phi_{n}]=D^{-\frac{1}{2}}U`$. Thus,

|     |                                  |                                                             |     |        |
| --- | -------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- | --- | ------ |
|     | $`\displaystyle\Phi\Phi^{\top}`$ | $`\displaystyle=D^{-\frac{1}{2}}UU^{\top}D^{-\frac{1}{2}}`$ |     | (B.35) |
|     |                                  | $`\displaystyle=D^{-1}`$                                    |     | (B.36) |

Denoting $`n:=|V|`$, for any $`u,v\in V`$,

|                                                                                                           |                                                                        |                                                   |     |        |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- | --- | ------ |
|                                                                                                           | $`\displaystyle\sum_{i=1}^{n}\phi_{i}(u)\phi_{i}(v)`$                  | $`\displaystyle=\frac{1[u=v]}{\pi(v)}`$           |     | (B.37) |
|                                                                                                           | $`\displaystyle\sum_{i=1}^{n}\bigl(\phi_{i}(u)-\phi_{i}(v)\bigr)^{2}`$ | $`\displaystyle=\begin{cases}0,&u=v,\\[2.84526pt] |
| \frac{1}{\pi(u)}+\frac{1}{\pi(v)},&u\neq v,\end{cases}\leq\frac{2}{\pi*{\min}}\mathbf{1}*{\{u\neq v\}}.`$ |                                                                        | (B.38)                                            |

Now

|     |                 |                     |                                           |                         |
| --- | --------------- | ------------------- | ----------------------------------------- | ----------------------- | ----------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --- | ----------------------- | --- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --- | ------ |
|     | $`\displaystyle |                     | \Phi*{t}^{\leq k}(u)-\Phi*{t}^{\leq k}(v) |                         | \_{2}^{2}`$ | $`\displaystyle=                                                                    |     | \Phi*{t}(u)-\Phi*{t}(v) |     | _{2}^{2}-\sum_{i\geq k+1}\lambda*{i}^{2t}\bigl(\phi*{i}(u)-\phi\_{i}(v)\bigr)^{2}`$ |     | (B.39) |
|     |                 | $`\displaystyle\geq |                                           | \Phi*{t}(u)-\Phi*{t}(v) |             | _{2}^{2}-\lambda_{k+1}^{2t}\sum*{i=1}^{n}\bigl(\phi*{i}(u)-\phi\_{i}(v)\bigr)^{2}`$ |     | (B.40)                  |
|     |                 | $`\displaystyle\geq |                                           | \Phi*{t}(u)-\Phi*{t}(v) |             | _{2}^{2}-\frac{2\lambda_{k+1}^{2t}}{\pi*{\min}}\mathbf{1}*{\{u\neq v\}}.`$          |     | (B.41)                  |

The upper bound
$`||\Phi_{t}^{\leq k}(u)-\Phi_{t}^{\leq k}(v)||_{2}^{2}\leq||\Phi_{t}(u)-\Phi_{t}(v)||_{2}^{2}`$
is immediate, since truncation only removes nonnegative terms. This
proves
[Equation B.32](#A2.E32 "In Lemma B.5. ‣ B.1.3 The Connection Between Diffusion Embeddings and Contrastive Learning ‣ B.1 Preliminary Lemmas ‣ Appendix B Theorems about Diffusion Similarity and Contrastive Learning ‣ A Theoretical Framework for Self-Play Theorem Proving Algorithms").

Similarly,

|     |                 |                     |                       |              |
| --- | --------------- | ------------------- | --------------------- | ------------ | ----------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- | --- | ------------ | --- | ---------------------------------------------------------- | --- | ------ |
|     | $`\displaystyle |                     | \Phi\_{t}^{\leq k}(v) |              | \_{2}^{2}`$ | $`\displaystyle=                                           |     | \Phi\_{t}(v) |     | _{2}^{2}-\sum_{i\geq k+1}\lambda*{i}^{2t}\phi*{i}(v)^{2}`$ |     | (B.42) |
|     |                 | $`\displaystyle\geq |                       | \Phi\_{t}(v) |             | _{2}^{2}-\lambda_{k+1}^{2t}\sum*{i=1}^{n}\phi*{i}(v)^{2}`$ |     | (B.43)       |
|     |                 | $`\displaystyle\geq |                       | \Phi\_{t}(v) |             | _{2}^{2}-\frac{\lambda_{k+1}^{2t}}{\pi\_{\min}}.`$         |     | (B.44)       |

Again, since truncation only removes nonnegative terms,
$`||\Phi_{t}^{\leq k}(v)||_{2}^{2}\leq||\Phi_{t}(v)||_{2}^{2}.`$ This
proves
[Equation B.33](#A2.E33 "In Lemma B.5. ‣ B.1.3 The Connection Between Diffusion Embeddings and Contrastive Learning ‣ B.1 Preliminary Lemmas ‣ Appendix B Theorems about Diffusion Similarity and Contrastive Learning ‣ A Theoretical Framework for Self-Play Theorem Proving Algorithms").

Finally,

|     |                                                                                              |                                                                                                                                                                                      |     |                   |
| --- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --- | ----------------- |
|     | $`\displaystyle\langle\Phi_{t}^{\leq k}(u),\Phi_{t}^{\leq k}(v)\rangle`$                     | $`\displaystyle=\langle\Phi_{t}(u),\Phi_{t}(v)\rangle-\sum_{i\geq k+1}\lambda_{i}^{2t}\phi_{i}(u)\phi_{i}(v)`$                                                                       |     | (B.45)            |
|     |                                                                                              | $`\displaystyle\geq\langle\Phi_{t}(u),\Phi_{t}(v)\rangle-\sqrt{\Big(\sum_{i\geq k+1}\lambda_{i}^{2t}\phi_{i}(u)^{2}\Big)\Big(\sum_{i\geq k+1}\lambda_{i}^{2t}\phi_{i}(v)^{2}\Big)}`$ |     | (Cauchy Schwartz) |
|     |                                                                                              | $`\displaystyle\geq\langle\Phi_{t}(u),\Phi_{t}(v)\rangle-\lambda_{k+1}^{2t}\sqrt{\Big(\sum_{i=1}^{n}\phi_{i}(u)^{2}\Big)\Big(\sum_{i=1}^{n}\phi_{i}(v)^{2}\Big)}`$                   |     | (B.46)            |
|     |                                                                                              | $`\displaystyle\geq\langle\Phi_{t}(u),\Phi_{t}(v)\rangle-\frac{\lambda_{k+1}^{2t}}{\pi_{\textup{min}}}`$                                                                             |     | (B.47)            |
|     | $`\displaystyle\textup{Similarly, }\langle\Phi_{t}^{\leq k}(u),\Phi_{t}^{\leq k}(v)\rangle`$ | $`\displaystyle\leq\langle\Phi_{t}(u),\Phi_{t}(v)\rangle+\frac{\lambda_{k+1}^{2t}}{\pi_{\textup{min}}}`$                                                                             |     | (B.48)            |

∎

We will now describe how to learn the embeddings
$`\{\Phi_{t}^{\leq k}(u)\}_{u\in V}`$ for general $`k\in[|V|]`$ and
$`t\in\mathbb{N}`$.
[Lemma B.6](#A2.Thmtheorem6 "Lemma B.6 (Global Minimizers for Contrastive Loss). ‣ B.1.3 The Connection Between Diffusion Embeddings and Contrastive Learning ‣ B.1 Preliminary Lemmas ‣ Appendix B Theorems about Diffusion Similarity and Contrastive Learning ‣ A Theoretical Framework for Self-Play Theorem Proving Algorithms")
shows the global minimizers of the contrastive loss recover
$`\{\Phi^{\leq k}_{t}(u)\}_{u\in V}`$ up to an orthogonal
transformation.

###### Lemma B.6 (Global Minimizers for Contrastive Loss).

Let $`G=(V,E)`$ be any connected, undirected graph. Let $`(V,P)`$ be a
reversible Markov chain with transition matrix
$`P\in[0,1]^{|V|\times|V|}`$ and stationary measure $`\pi\in\Delta(V)`$.
Let $`\{\lambda_{i}(P)\}_{i\in[|V|]}`$ be the eigenvalues of $`P`$,
ordered by decreasing absolute value. Fix any $`t\in\mathbb{N}`$ and
$`k\in[|V|]`$. Suppose $`|\lambda_{k}(P)|-|\lambda_{k+1}(P)|>0`$ if
$`k<|V|`$ and suppose the population contrastive loss
([Equation B.12](#A2.E12 "In B.1.1 Setup ‣ B.1 Preliminary Lemmas ‣ Appendix B Theorems about Diffusion Similarity and Contrastive Learning ‣ A Theoretical Framework for Self-Play Theorem Proving Algorithms"))
with base distribution $`\pi`$, augmentation function $`P^{t}`$, and
embedding dimension $`k`$ has a global minimizer in
$`\mathcal{F}_{\textup{emb}}`$. Then, for any such global minimizer
$`\mathcal{F}_{\textup{emb}}\ni h_{\theta_{*}}:V\to\mathbb{R}^{k}`$,
there exists an orthogonal matrix $`R_{*}\in O^{k\times k}`$ where

|     |                                                                                                |     |        |
| --- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --- | ------ |
|     | $`\displaystyle\forall u\in V,h_{\theta_{*}}(u)=R_{*}\,\Phi^{\leq k}_{t}(u)\in\mathbb{R}^{k}`$ |     | (B.49) |

With mapping $`C:V\to\Delta(V)`$ defined as the sampler-representation
of $`P`$, where $`\forall x\in V,C(x)=P[x]`$, then the positive and
negative pair distribution corresponding to base distribution $`\pi`$
and augmentation function $`P^{t}`$ are where positive pairs $`(x,y)`$
are generated by sampling $`z\sim\pi,`$ then
$`x\sim C^{t}(z),y\sim C^{t}(z)`$ independently. Negative pairs
$`(x,y)`$ are generated via $`x,y\sim\pi`$ independently. Note that
$`\sigma_{x}`$ (defined in
[Equation B.5](#A2.E5 "In B.1.1 Setup ‣ B.1 Preliminary Lemmas ‣ Appendix B Theorems about Diffusion Similarity and Contrastive Learning ‣ A Theoretical Framework for Self-Play Theorem Proving Algorithms"))
equals $`\pi(x)`$ for every $`x\in V`$.

###### Proof.

Fix $`t\in\mathbb{N}`$ and $`k\in[|V|]`$. The plan is to follow the
derivation process of the contrastive loss
$`\mathcal{L}_{\textup{cont}}`$, but with $`\mu=\pi`$ and $`Q=P^{t}`$.
First, we have

|     |                               |                                                                           |     |                                |
| --- | ----------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --- | ------------------------------ |
|     | $`\displaystyle A`$           | $`\displaystyle=Q^{\top}\textup{diag}(\mu)Q`$                             |     | (B.50)                         |
|     |                               | $`\displaystyle=(P^{t})^{\top}\textup{diag}(\pi)P^{t}`$                   |     | (B.51)                         |
|     |                               | $`\displaystyle=\textup{diag}(\pi)P^{2t}`$                                |     | (By reversibility of $`P`$)    |
|     | $`\displaystyle D`$           | $`\displaystyle:=\textup{diag}(A\mathbf{1})`$                             |     | (B.52)                         |
|     |                               | $`\displaystyle=\textup{diag}(\pi)`$                                      |     | (Row sums of $`P^{2t}`$ are 1) |
|     | $`\displaystyle\overline{A}`$ | $`\displaystyle:=D^{-1/2}AD^{-1/2}`$                                      |     | (B.53)                         |
|     |                               | $`\displaystyle=\textup{diag}(\pi)^{1/2}P^{2t}\textup{diag}(\pi)^{-1/2}`$ |     | (B.54)                         |

Let the eigendecomposition of $`\overline{A}`$ be
$`\overline{A}=\sum_{i\in[|V|]}\lambda_{i}(\overline{A})\,u_{i}u_{i}^{\top}=U\Lambda U^{\top}`$.
By the Eckart-Young-Mirsky Theorem \[[13](#bib.bib39)\], since
$`\overline{A}`$ is p.s.d. and
$`\lambda_{k}(\overline{A})-\lambda_{k+1}(\overline{A})=\lambda_{k}(P)^{2t}-\lambda_{k+1}(P)^{2t}>0`$
if $`k<|V|`$, the rank-$`k`$ minimizers of the matrix factorization loss
are:

|     |                                                                                   |     |            |
| --- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --- | ---------- | --- | ---------------------- | --- | ----------- | --- | ------ |
|     | $`\displaystyle\{U\Lambda^{1/2}R:R\in O^{k\times k}\}=\arg\min\_{F\in\mathbb{R}^{ | V   | \times k}} |     | \overline{A}-FF^{\top} |     | \_{F}^{2}`$ |     | (B.55) |

Because for any $`h_{\theta}\in\mathcal{F}_{\textup{emb}}`$,
$`\mathcal{L}_{\textup{mf}}(h_{\theta})=\mathcal{L}_{\textup{cont}}(h_{\theta})+c`$
for some constant $`c`$ independent of $`h_{\theta}`$
([Equation B.10](#A2.E10 "In B.1.1 Setup ‣ B.1 Preliminary Lemmas ‣ Appendix B Theorems about Diffusion Similarity and Contrastive Learning ‣ A Theoretical Framework for Self-Play Theorem Proving Algorithms")),
then if $`\mathcal{F}_{\textup{emb}}`$ contains some
$`h_{\theta_{*}}:V\to\mathbb{R}^{k}`$ which is a global minimizer of
$`\mathcal{L}_{\textup{cont}}`$, then the induced matrix
$`F_{\theta_{*}}\in\mathbb{R}^{|V|\times k}`$, where the $`x`$-th row
is:

|     |                                                   |                                                         |     |        |
| --- | ------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- | --- | ------ |
|     | $`\displaystyle\forall x\in V,F_{\theta_{*}}[x]`$ | $`\displaystyle=\sqrt{\pi(x)}h_{\theta_{*}}(x)^{\top}`$ |     | (B.56) |

Must be in the set
$`\arg\min_{F\in\mathbb{R}^{|V|\times k}}||\overline{A}-FF^{\top}||_{F}^{2}=\{U\Lambda^{1/2}R:R\in O^{k\times k}\}`$.
In particular, there exists $`R\in O^{k\times k}`$ where

|     |                                                  |     |        |
| --- | ------------------------------------------------ | --- | ------ |
|     | $`\displaystyle F_{\theta_{*}}=U\Lambda^{1/2}R`$ |     | (B.57) |

The $`x`$-th row of $`U\Lambda^{1/2}R`$ is
$`(\lambda_{i}(\overline{A})^{1/2}u_{i}(x))_{i\in[k]}^{\top}R\in\mathbb{R}^{1\times k}`$,
where $`u_{i}(x)`$ is the $`x`$-th entry of $`u_{i}`$. Thus,

|     |                                                     |                                                                                                 |     |        |
| --- | --------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --- | ------ |
|     | $`\displaystyle\forall x\in V,\,h_{\theta_{*}}(x)`$ | $`\displaystyle=(\pi(x))^{-1/2}R\,(\lambda_{i}(\overline{A})^{1/2}u_{i}(x))_{i\in[k]}`$         |     | (B.58) |
|     |                                                     | $`\displaystyle=R\,\Big(\lambda_{i}(\overline{A})^{1/2}(\pi(x))^{-1/2}u_{i}(x)\Big)_{i\in[k]}`$ |     | (B.59) |

Finally, we note that since
$`\{(\lambda_{i}(\overline{A}),u_{i})\}_{i\in[k]}`$ are the top $`k`$
eigenvalue and eigenvectors of
$`\overline{A}=\textup{diag}(\pi)^{1/2}P^{2t}\textup{diag}(\pi)^{-1/2}`$,
then the eigendecomposition of $`P^{2t}`$ is:

|     |                          |                              |     |                                                                                                                      |
| --- | ------------------------ | ---------------------------- | --- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --- | ------ |
|     | $`\displaystyle P^{2t}`$ | $`\displaystyle=\sum\_{i\in[ | V   | ]}\lambda*{i}(\overline{A})\big(\textup{diag}(\pi)^{-1/2}u*{i}\big)\big(\textup{diag}(\pi)^{1/2}u\_{i}\big)^{\top}`$ |     | (B.60) |
|     |                          | $`\displaystyle=\sum\_{i\in[ | V   | ]}(\lambda*{i}(P))^{2t}\big(\textup{diag}(\pi)^{-1/2}u*{i}\big)\big(\textup{diag}(\pi)^{1/2}u\_{i}\big)^{\top}`$     |     | (B.61) |

Where $`\{\lambda_{i}(P)\}_{i\in[|V|]}`$ are the eigenvalues of $`P`$
arranged in decreasing order of absolute value, so that
$`\lambda_{i}(\overline{A})^{1/2}=|\lambda_{i}(P)|^{t}`$. Finally, we
see that the right eigenvectors of $`P^{2t}`$ are exactly
$`\{\textup{diag}(\pi)^{-1/2}u_{i}\}_{i\in[|V|]}`$. Thus,
[Equation B.59](#A2.E59 "In Proof. ‣ B.1.3 The Connection Between Diffusion Embeddings and Contrastive Learning ‣ B.1 Preliminary Lemmas ‣ Appendix B Theorems about Diffusion Similarity and Contrastive Learning ‣ A Theoretical Framework for Self-Play Theorem Proving Algorithms")
can be written in terms of the $`k`$ truncated spectral diffusion
embedding in
[Definition B.3](#A2.Thmtheorem3 "Definition B.3. ‣ B.1.3 The Connection Between Diffusion Embeddings and Contrastive Learning ‣ B.1 Preliminary Lemmas ‣ Appendix B Theorems about Diffusion Similarity and Contrastive Learning ‣ A Theoretical Framework for Self-Play Theorem Proving Algorithms").

|     |                                                     |                                                                                                           |     |        |
| --- | --------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --- | ------ |
|     | $`\displaystyle\forall x\in V,\,h_{\theta_{*}}(x)`$ | $`\displaystyle=R\,\Big(\lambda_{i}(\overline{A})^{1/2}(\pi(x))^{-1/2}u_{i}(x)\Big)_{i\in[k]}`$           |     | (B.62) |
|     |                                                     | $`\displaystyle=R\,\textup{diag}(\textup{sign}(\{\lambda_{i}(P)^{t}\}_{i\in[k]}))\,\Phi_{t}^{\leq k}(x)`$ |     | (B.63) |
|     |                                                     | $`\displaystyle=R_{*}\,\Phi_{t}^{\leq k}(x)`$                                                             |     | (B.64) |

Where
$`\textup{diag}(\textup{sign}(\{\lambda_{i}(P)^{t}\}_{i\in[k]}))\in O^{k\times k}`$
is a diagonal matrix where the $`(i,i)`$-th entry is $`1`$ if
$`\lambda_{i}(P)^{t}`$ is non-negative, and $`-1`$ if
$`\lambda_{i}(P)^{t}`$ is negative, for $`i\in[k]`$. Since
$`R,\,\textup{diag}(\textup{sign}(\{\lambda_{i}(P)^{t}\}_{i\in[k]}))\in O^{k\times k}`$,
then
$`R_{*}:=R\,\textup{diag}(\textup{sign}(\{\lambda_{i}(P)^{t}\}_{i\in[k]}))\in O^{k\times k}`$.

∎

###### Corollary B.7.

Let $`G=(V,E)`$ be any connected, undirected graph. Let $`(V,P)`$ be a
reversible Markov chain with transition matrix
$`P\in[0,1]^{|V|\times|V|}`$ and stationary measure $`\pi`$. Fix any
$`t\in\mathbb{N}`$ and $`k\in[|V|]`$. Let
$`\{\lambda_{i}(P)\}_{i\in[|V|]}`$ be the eigenvalues of $`P`$, ordered
by decreasing absolute value. Suppose
$`|\lambda_{k}(P)|-|\lambda_{k+1}(P)|>0`$ if $`k<|V|`$. Denote
$`\mathcal{F}_{\textup{emb}}^{(k)}\subset\mathcal{F}_{V}^{(k)}`$ as a
class of embedding models from $`V`$ to $`\mathbb{R}^{k}`$ and
$`\mathcal{F}_{\textup{emb}}^{(|V|)}\subset\mathcal{F}_{V}^{(|V|)}`$ a
class of embedding models from $`V`$ to $`\mathbb{R}^{|V|}`$. Suppose
the population contrastive loss
([Equation B.12](#A2.E12 "In B.1.1 Setup ‣ B.1 Preliminary Lemmas ‣ Appendix B Theorems about Diffusion Similarity and Contrastive Learning ‣ A Theoretical Framework for Self-Play Theorem Proving Algorithms"))
with base distribution $`\pi`$, augmentation function $`P^{t}`$, and
embedding dimension $`k`$ (dimension $`|V|`$) has a global minimizer in
$`\mathcal{F}_{\textup{emb}}^{(k)}`$
($`\mathcal{F}_{\textup{emb}}^{(|V|)}`$).

Let $`\theta_{*}`$ be any global minimizer of the population contrastive
loss with embedding dimension $`|V|`$, and $`\theta_{*}^{(k)}`$ be any
global minimizer of the population contrastive loss with embedding
dimension with embedding dimension $`k`$. There exist orthogonal
matrices $`R\in O^{|V|\times|V|}`$ and $`R^{(k)}\in O^{k\times k}`$ such
that $`\forall u\in V,`$

|     |                                           |                                                                  |     |        |
| --- | ----------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- | --- | ------ | --- | ------ |
|     | $`\displaystyle h_{\theta_{*}^{(k)}}(u)`$ | $`\displaystyle=R^{(k)}\,\Phi^{\leq k}_{t}(u)\in\mathbb{R}^{k}`$ |     | (B.65) |
|     | $`\displaystyle h_{\theta_{*}}(u)`$       | $`\displaystyle=R\,\Phi\_{t}(u)\in\mathbb{R}^{                   | V   | }`$    |     | (B.66) |

In particular, $`\forall u,v\in V,`$ with
$`\pi_{\textup{min}}:=\min_{v\in V}\pi(v)`$,

|     |                 |                     |                                     |                                                 |
| --- | --------------- | ------------------- | ----------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------ | --- | ----------------------------------------- | --- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --- | ------------------ | --- | ----------- | --- | ------ |
|     | $`\displaystyle |                     | h*{\theta*{_}}(u)-h*{\theta*{_}}(v) |                                                 | ^{2}-\frac{2(\lambda*{k+1}(P))^{2t}}{\pi*{\textup{min}}}`$     | $`\displaystyle=         |     | p^{t}(u)-p^{t}(v)                         |     | ^{2}_{\ell^{2}(1/\pi)}-\frac{2(\lambda_{k+1}(P))^{2t}}{\pi\_{\textup{min}}}`$ |     | (B.67)             |
|     |                 | $`\displaystyle\leq |                                     | h*{\theta*{_}^{(k)}}(u)-h*{\theta*{_}^{(k)}}(v) |                                                                | ^{2}\_{2}=               |     | \Phi^{\leq k}_{t}(u)-\Phi^{\leq k}_{t}(v) |     | ^{2}\_{2}`$                                                                   |     | (B.68)             |
|     |                 | $`\displaystyle\leq |                                     | p^{t}(u)-p^{t}(v)                               |                                                                | ^{2}\_{\ell^{2}(1/\pi)}= |     | h*{\theta*{_}}(u)-h*{\theta*{_}}(v)       |     | ^{2}`$                                                                        |     | (B.69)             |
|     | $`\displaystyle |                     | h*{\theta*{\*}}(v)                  |                                                 | _{2}^{2}-\frac{(\lambda_{k+1}(P))^{2t}}{\pi\_{\textup{min}}}`$ | $`\displaystyle\leq      |     | h*{\theta*{_}^{k\_{_}}}(v)                |     | \_{2}^{2}\leq                                                                 |     | h*{\theta*{\*}}(v) |     | \_{2}^{2}`$ |     | (B.70) |

###### Proof.

We apply
[Lemma B.6](#A2.Thmtheorem6 "Lemma B.6 (Global Minimizers for Contrastive Loss). ‣ B.1.3 The Connection Between Diffusion Embeddings and Contrastive Learning ‣ B.1 Preliminary Lemmas ‣ Appendix B Theorems about Diffusion Similarity and Contrastive Learning ‣ A Theoretical Framework for Self-Play Theorem Proving Algorithms")
with graph $`G`$ and with embedding dimension $`k`$ (resp. embedding
dimension $`|V|)`$ to get
[Equation B.65](#A2.E65 "In Corollary B.7. ‣ B.1.3 The Connection Between Diffusion Embeddings and Contrastive Learning ‣ B.1 Preliminary Lemmas ‣ Appendix B Theorems about Diffusion Similarity and Contrastive Learning ‣ A Theoretical Framework for Self-Play Theorem Proving Algorithms")
(resp.
[Equation B.66](#A2.E66 "In Corollary B.7. ‣ B.1.3 The Connection Between Diffusion Embeddings and Contrastive Learning ‣ B.1 Preliminary Lemmas ‣ Appendix B Theorems about Diffusion Similarity and Contrastive Learning ‣ A Theoretical Framework for Self-Play Theorem Proving Algorithms")).
[Equation B.69](#A2.E69 "In Corollary B.7. ‣ B.1.3 The Connection Between Diffusion Embeddings and Contrastive Learning ‣ B.1 Preliminary Lemmas ‣ Appendix B Theorems about Diffusion Similarity and Contrastive Learning ‣ A Theoretical Framework for Self-Play Theorem Proving Algorithms")
is obtained by combining
[Equation B.65](#A2.E65 "In Corollary B.7. ‣ B.1.3 The Connection Between Diffusion Embeddings and Contrastive Learning ‣ B.1 Preliminary Lemmas ‣ Appendix B Theorems about Diffusion Similarity and Contrastive Learning ‣ A Theoretical Framework for Self-Play Theorem Proving Algorithms"),
[Equation B.66](#A2.E66 "In Corollary B.7. ‣ B.1.3 The Connection Between Diffusion Embeddings and Contrastive Learning ‣ B.1 Preliminary Lemmas ‣ Appendix B Theorems about Diffusion Similarity and Contrastive Learning ‣ A Theoretical Framework for Self-Play Theorem Proving Algorithms"),
[Lemma B.4](#A2.Thmtheorem4 "Lemma B.4 (Diffusion Embeddings). ‣ B.1.3 The Connection Between Diffusion Embeddings and Contrastive Learning ‣ B.1 Preliminary Lemmas ‣ Appendix B Theorems about Diffusion Similarity and Contrastive Learning ‣ A Theoretical Framework for Self-Play Theorem Proving Algorithms"),
and
[Lemma B.5](#A2.Thmtheorem5 "Lemma B.5. ‣ B.1.3 The Connection Between Diffusion Embeddings and Contrastive Learning ‣ B.1 Preliminary Lemmas ‣ Appendix B Theorems about Diffusion Similarity and Contrastive Learning ‣ A Theoretical Framework for Self-Play Theorem Proving Algorithms").
[Equation B.70](#A2.E70 "In Corollary B.7. ‣ B.1.3 The Connection Between Diffusion Embeddings and Contrastive Learning ‣ B.1 Preliminary Lemmas ‣ Appendix B Theorems about Diffusion Similarity and Contrastive Learning ‣ A Theoretical Framework for Self-Play Theorem Proving Algorithms")
is obtained by combining
[Lemma B.5](#A2.Thmtheorem5 "Lemma B.5. ‣ B.1.3 The Connection Between Diffusion Embeddings and Contrastive Learning ‣ B.1 Preliminary Lemmas ‣ Appendix B Theorems about Diffusion Similarity and Contrastive Learning ‣ A Theoretical Framework for Self-Play Theorem Proving Algorithms")
with
[Equation B.65](#A2.E65 "In Corollary B.7. ‣ B.1.3 The Connection Between Diffusion Embeddings and Contrastive Learning ‣ B.1 Preliminary Lemmas ‣ Appendix B Theorems about Diffusion Similarity and Contrastive Learning ‣ A Theoretical Framework for Self-Play Theorem Proving Algorithms")
and
[Equation B.66](#A2.E66 "In Corollary B.7. ‣ B.1.3 The Connection Between Diffusion Embeddings and Contrastive Learning ‣ B.1 Preliminary Lemmas ‣ Appendix B Theorems about Diffusion Similarity and Contrastive Learning ‣ A Theoretical Framework for Self-Play Theorem Proving Algorithms").
