#### B.1.4 Matrix Factorization Lemmas

[Lemma B.4](#A2.Thmtheorem4 "Lemma B.4 (Diffusion Embeddings). ‣ B.1.3 The Connection Between Diffusion Embeddings and Contrastive Learning ‣ B.1 Preliminary Lemmas ‣ Appendix B Theorems about Diffusion Similarity and Contrastive Learning ‣ A Theoretical Framework for Self-Play Theorem Proving Algorithms")
and
[Lemma B.6](#A2.Thmtheorem6 "Lemma B.6 (Global Minimizers for Contrastive Loss). ‣ B.1.3 The Connection Between Diffusion Embeddings and Contrastive Learning ‣ B.1 Preliminary Lemmas ‣ Appendix B Theorems about Diffusion Similarity and Contrastive Learning ‣ A Theoretical Framework for Self-Play Theorem Proving Algorithms")
motivate the idea of using embeddings learned via contrastive learning
to compute the diffusion similarity and distance.
[Lemma B.2](#A2.Thmtheorem2 "Lemma B.2 (Generalization of ERM). ‣ B.1.2 Lemmas on Contrastive Learning ‣ B.1 Preliminary Lemmas ‣ Appendix B Theorems about Diffusion Similarity and Contrastive Learning ‣ A Theoretical Framework for Self-Play Theorem Proving Algorithms")
shows that finding the ERM (or $`\frac{\epsilon}{2}`$-ERM) suffices,
with high probability, to find an $`\epsilon`$-minimizer of the
population contrastive loss $`\mathcal{L}_{\textup{cont}}`$.
[Lemma B.11](#A2.Thmtheorem11 "Lemma B.11 (Approximate minimizers are close to a global minimizer). ‣ B.1.4 Matrix Factorization Lemmas ‣ B.1 Preliminary Lemmas ‣ Appendix B Theorems about Diffusion Similarity and Contrastive Learning ‣ A Theoretical Framework for Self-Play Theorem Proving Algorithms"),
a Lemma about matrix-factorization, is useful in quantifying how close
an embedding corresponding to such an $`\epsilon`$-minimizer is to a
ground-truth embedding, up to a rotation.

To start,
[Lemma B.10](#A2.Thmtheorem10 "Lemma B.10. ‣ B.1.4 Matrix Factorization Lemmas ‣ B.1 Preliminary Lemmas ‣ Appendix B Theorems about Diffusion Similarity and Contrastive Learning ‣ A Theoretical Framework for Self-Play Theorem Proving Algorithms"),
[Lemma B.9](#A2.Thmtheorem9 "Lemma B.9. ‣ B.1.4 Matrix Factorization Lemmas ‣ B.1 Preliminary Lemmas ‣ Appendix B Theorems about Diffusion Similarity and Contrastive Learning ‣ A Theoretical Framework for Self-Play Theorem Proving Algorithms"),
and
[Lemma B.8](#A2.Thmtheorem8 "Lemma B.8. ‣ B.1.4 Matrix Factorization Lemmas ‣ B.1 Preliminary Lemmas ‣ Appendix B Theorems about Diffusion Similarity and Contrastive Learning ‣ A Theoretical Framework for Self-Play Theorem Proving Algorithms")
are introduced here to prove
[Lemma B.11](#A2.Thmtheorem11 "Lemma B.11 (Approximate minimizers are close to a global minimizer). ‣ B.1.4 Matrix Factorization Lemmas ‣ B.1 Preliminary Lemmas ‣ Appendix B Theorems about Diffusion Similarity and Contrastive Learning ‣ A Theoretical Framework for Self-Play Theorem Proving Algorithms").
Note that for two matrices
$`A,B\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n},\langle A,B\rangle:=\mathrm{tr}(A^{\top}B)`$
denotes the Hilbert-Schmidt inner product of the two matrices, with
$`||A||_{F}^{2}=\langle A,A\rangle`$.

###### Lemma B.8.

(Lemma 5.4 of \[[34](#bib.bib7)\]) For any natural numbers $`n\geq k`$
and matrices $`U,X\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times k}`$,

|     |                                                                   |     |      |
| --- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- | --- | ---- | --- | ---------------------------------------------------- | --- | ------------------- | --- | ------------ | --- | ------ |
|     | $`\displaystyle\textup{dist}(U,X)^{2}:=\min\_{R\in O^{k\times k}} |     | U-XR |     | _{F}^{2}\leq\frac{1}{2(\sqrt{2}-1)\sigma_{k}(X)^{2}} |     | UU^{\top}-XX^{\top} |     | \_{F}^{2}.`$ |     | (B.71) |

###### Lemma B.9.

(Ky Fan Maximum Principle \[[14](#bib.bib37)\]; Theorem 1 of
\[[29](#bib.bib38)\]) Let $`A`$ be a real, symmetric $`n\times n`$
matrix, with eigenvalues $`\lambda_{1}\geq\ldots\geq\lambda_{n}`$. For
any $`k\in[n]`$,

|     |                                                                                          |     |        |
| --- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --- | ------ |
|     | $`\displaystyle\max_{X^{\top}X=I_{k}}\mathrm{tr}(X^{\top}AX)=\sum_{i=1}^{k}\lambda_{i}`$ |     | (B.72) |

###### Lemma B.10.

(Lemma 3.1 of \[[36](#bib.bib9)\]) Let $`A\in R^{n\times n}`$ be a
symmetric matrix, with eigenvalues ordered as
$`|\lambda_{1}|\geq|\lambda_{2}|\geq\ldots\geq|\lambda_{n}|`$. For
$`k\in[n-1]`$, let $`P_{k}`$ be the projector onto the subspace spanned
by the top-$`k`$ eigenvectors of $`A`$, denoted
$`\lambda_{1},\ldots,\lambda_{k}`$. Assume that
$`\lambda_{k}^{2}-\lambda_{k+1}^{2}>0`$. For any symmetric rank-$`k`$
projector $`P\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}`$, $`P^{\top}=P`$, $`P^{2}=P`$,
$`\mathrm{tr}(P)=k`$, we have:

|     |                                                                                             |     |          |
| --- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --- | -------- | --- | ------------ | --- | ------ |
|     | $`\displaystyle\langle A^{2},P*{k}-P\rangle\geq\frac{\lambda*{k}^{2}-\lambda\_{k+1}^{2}}{2} |     | P\_{k}-P |     | \_{F}^{2}.`$ |     | (B.73) |

###### Proof.

Diagonalize
$`A^{2}=U\textup{diag}(\{\lambda_{i}^{2}\}_{i\in[n]})U^{\top}`$ and
write $`\widetilde{P}:=U^{\top}PU`$. Partition $`\widetilde{P}`$ as

|                                                                                |                                                             |        |     |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------- | ------ | --- |
|                                                                                | $`\displaystyle\widetilde{P}=\begin{pmatrix}P*{11}&P*{12}\\ |
| P*{21}&P*{22}\end{pmatrix}\quad\text{with }P\_{11}\in\mathbb{R}^{k\times k}.`$ |                                                             | (B.74) |

Then $`\widetilde{P}_{k}=U^{\top}P_{k}U=\textup{diag}(I_{k},0)`$ in the
eigenbasis, and

|     |                                               |                                                                                                                      |     |        |
| --- | --------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --- | ------ |
|     | $`\displaystyle\langle A^{2},P_{k}-P\rangle`$ | $`\displaystyle=\mathrm{tr}\big(\textup{diag}(\{\lambda_{i}^{2}\}_{i\in[n]})(\widetilde{P}_{k}-\widetilde{P})\big)`$ |     | (B.75) |
|     |                                               | $`\displaystyle=\mathrm{tr}\big(\Lambda_{k}^{2}(I-P_{11})\big)-\mathrm{tr}\big(\Lambda_{\perp}^{2}P_{22}\big)`$      |     | (B.76) |

where
$`\Lambda_{\perp}:=\textup{diag}(\{\lambda_{k+1},\dots,\lambda_{n}\})`$.
Using $`\Lambda_{k}^{2}\succeq\lambda_{k}^{2}I_{k}`$ and
$`\Lambda_{\perp}^{2}\preceq\lambda_{k+1}^{2}I`$ gives

|     |                                                                                                                             |     |        |
| --- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --- | ------ |
|     | $`\displaystyle\langle A^{2},P_{k}-P\rangle\geq\lambda_{k}^{2}\mathrm{tr}(I-P_{11})-\lambda_{k+1}^{2}\mathrm{tr}(P_{22}).`$ |     | (B.77) |

Since $`\widetilde{P}`$ is a rank-$`k`$ projector,
$`\mathrm{tr}(\widetilde{P})=k`$, so
$`\mathrm{tr}(P_{11})+\mathrm{tr}(P_{22})=k`$ and thus
$`\mathrm{tr}(I-P_{11})=\mathrm{tr}(P_{22})`$. Also, for rank-$`k`$
projectors,

|     |                 |                                                                          |          |        |
| --- | --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------- | ------ | ----------- | ---------------------------------------------------- | --- | ------ |
|     | $`\displaystyle |                                                                          | P\_{k}-P |        | \_{F}^{2}`$ | $`\displaystyle=\mathrm{tr}\big((P_{k}-P)^{2}\big)`$ |     | (B.78) |
|     |                 | $`\displaystyle=\mathrm{tr}(P_{k})+\mathrm{tr}(P)-2\mathrm{tr}(P_{k}P)`$ |          | (B.79) |
|     |                 | $`\displaystyle=2k-2\mathrm{tr}(P_{11})`$                                |          | (B.80) |
|     |                 | $`\displaystyle=2\mathrm{tr}(I-P_{11}).`$                                |          | (B.81) |

Therefore $`\mathrm{tr}(I-P_{11})=\frac{1}{2}||P_{k}-P||_{F}^{2}`$, and
we obtain
[Equation B.73](#A2.E73 "In Lemma B.10. ‣ B.1.4 Matrix Factorization Lemmas ‣ B.1 Preliminary Lemmas ‣ Appendix B Theorems about Diffusion Similarity and Contrastive Learning ‣ A Theoretical Framework for Self-Play Theorem Proving Algorithms").
∎

###### Lemma B.11 (Approximate minimizers are close to a global minimizer).

Let $`A\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}`$ be symmetric positive semidefinite
with eigendecomposition
$`A=U\textup{diag}(\{\lambda_{i}\}_{i\in[n]})U^{\top}`$ where
$`\lambda_{1}\geq\cdots\geq\lambda_{n}\geq 0`$. Fix $`1\leq k<n`$ and
assume $`\lambda_{k}>0`$ and the squared eigengap
$`\lambda_{k}^{2}-\lambda_{k+1}^{2}>0.`$ Define, for matrix
$`F\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times k}`$ of rank $`k`$,

|     |                                 |                   |     |             |
| --- | ------------------------------- | ----------------- | --- | ----------- | --- | ----------- | --- | ------ |
|     | $`\displaystyle\mathcal{L}(F)`$ | $`\displaystyle:= |     | A-FF^{\top} |     | \_{F}^{2}`$ |     | (B.82) |

Suppose $`F\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times k}`$ satisfies
$`\mathcal{L}(F)\leq\min_{\textup{rank}(Z)=k}\mathcal{L}(Z)+\epsilon`$
for some $`0<\epsilon\leq 1.`$ Define the constant
$`\mathcal{C}(A,k):=\frac{\Big(1+4||A||_{2}\sqrt{\frac{2}{\lambda_{k}^{2}-\lambda_{k+1}^{2}}}\Big)^{2}}{2(\sqrt{2}-1)\lambda_{k}}`$.
Then, there exists a global minimizer
$`F^{*}\in\arg\min_{\textup{rank}(Z)=k}\mathcal{L}(Z)`$ such that:

|     |                 |     |          |     |
| --- | --------------- | --- | -------- | --- | ----------- | ----------------------------------------------- | --- | ------ |
|     | $`\displaystyle |     | F-F^{\*} |     | \_{F}^{2}`$ | $`\displaystyle\leq\mathcal{C}(A,k)\,\epsilon`$ |     | (B.83) |

###### Proof.

First, we recall the Eckart-Young-Mirsky Theorem \[[13](#bib.bib39)\],
which characterizes the global minima of the loss function
$`\mathcal{L}(F)`$. Let $`U_{k}\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times k}`$ be the first
$`k`$ eigenvectors and let
$`\Lambda_{k}:=\textup{diag}(\lambda_{1},\dots,\lambda_{k})`$. Since
$`A\succeq 0`$ and $`\lambda_{k}^{2}-\lambda_{k+1}^{2}>0`$, the best
rank-$`k`$ approximation in Frobenius norm is
$`A_{k}:=U_{k}\Lambda_{k}U_{k}^{\top}`$, which is unique.

|     |                                                          |     |          |
| --- | -------------------------------------------------------- | --- | -------- | --- | ------------------------------------ | --- | --- | --- | ---------- | --- | ------------ | --- | ------------ | --- | ------ |
|     | $`\displaystyle\min\_{\textup{rank}(Z)=k}\mathcal{L}(Z)= |     | A-A\_{k} |     | _{F}^{2}=\sum_{i>k}\lambda\_{i}^{2}= |     | A   |     | \_{F}^{2}- |     | \Lambda\_{k} |     | \_{F}^{2}.`$ |     | (B.84) |

Because of this, the set of global minimizers of $`\mathcal{L}(\cdot)`$
over rank-$`k`$, $`(n\times k)`$ matrices are
$`S:=\{U_{k}\Lambda_{k}^{1/2}R:R\in O^{k\times k}\}`$. With this, the
proof plan is to upper bound $`||FF^{\top}-A_{k}||_{F}`$, and then apply
[Lemma B.8](#A2.Thmtheorem8 "Lemma B.8. ‣ B.1.4 Matrix Factorization Lemmas ‣ B.1 Preliminary Lemmas ‣ Appendix B Theorems about Diffusion Similarity and Contrastive Learning ‣ A Theoretical Framework for Self-Play Theorem Proving Algorithms")
to get the final result. To bound, $`||FF^{\top}-A_{k}||_{F}`$, define
$`P`$ as the rank-$`k`$ projector onto $`\textup{col}(F)`$.

|     |                     |                                                                       |     |        |
| --- | ------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- | --- | ------ |
|     | $`\displaystyle P`$ | $`\displaystyle:=F(F^{\top}F)^{-1}F^{\top}\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}`$ |     | (B.85) |
|     | $`\displaystyle Q`$ | $`\displaystyle:=F(F^{\top}F)^{-1/2}\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times k}`$       |     | (B.86) |

Where $`P=QQ^{\top}.`$ We will use the following decomposition, as a
result of the triangle inequality.

|     |                 |     |                  |
| --- | --------------- | --- | ---------------- | --- | --------- | --- | ------------- | --- | ------ | --- | ---------- | --- | ------- | --- | ------ |
|     | $`\displaystyle |     | FF^{\top}-A\_{k} |     | \_{F}\leq |     | FF^{\top}-PAP |     | \_{F}+ |     | PAP-A\_{k} |     | \_{F}`$ |     | (B.87) |

The remaining proof will be dedicated to bounding the terms
$`||FF^{\top}-PAP||_{F}`$ and $`||PAP-A_{k}||_{F}`$ individually.

Bounding $`||FF^{\top}-PAP||_{F}`$.

First, we will show that $`||FF^{\top}-PAP||_{F}\leq\sqrt{\epsilon}`$.
Towards this, we derive a useful identity for $`\mathcal{L}(F)`$,
culminating in
[Equation B.93](#A2.E93 "In Proof. ‣ B.1.4 Matrix Factorization Lemmas ‣ B.1 Preliminary Lemmas ‣ Appendix B Theorems about Diffusion Similarity and Contrastive Learning ‣ A Theoretical Framework for Self-Play Theorem Proving Algorithms").
A direct expansion of $`\mathcal{L}(F)`$ gives the identity

|     |                                 |                  |     |                         |
| --- | ------------------------------- | ---------------- | --- | ----------------------- | --- | ----------- | --- | ------ | --- | ----------------------------------------------- | --- | ------ |
|     | $`\displaystyle\mathcal{L}(F)`$ | $`\displaystyle= |     | (FF^{\top}-PAP)+(PAP-A) |     | \_{F}^{2}`$ |     | (B.88) |
|     |                                 | $`\displaystyle= |     | FF^{\top}-PAP           |     | \_{F}^{2}+  |     | PAP-A  |     | \_{F}^{2}+2\langle FF^{\top}-PAP,PAP-A\rangle`$ |     | (B.89) |
|     |                                 | $`\displaystyle= |     | FF^{\top}-PAP           |     | \_{F}^{2}+  |     | PAP-A  |     | \_{F}^{2}`$                                     |     | (B.90) |

Where the last equality is because
$`\langle FF^{\top}-PAP,PAP-A\rangle=\mathrm{tr}(FF^{\top}PAP-FF^{\top}A)+\mathrm{tr}(-(PAP)^{2}+PAPA)=0`$,
as $`\mathrm{tr}(FF^{\top}PAP)=\mathrm{tr}(FF^{\top}A)`$ and
$`\mathrm{tr}((PAP)^{2})=\mathrm{tr}(PAPA)`$. Subtracting
$`\min_{\textup{rank}(Z)=k}\mathcal{L}(Z)=||A||_{F}^{2}-||\Lambda_{k}||_{F}^{2}`$
yields

|     |                                                                         |                  |     |               |
| --- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------- | --- | ------------- | --- | ----------- | --- | ------------ | --- | ----------- | --- | ---------- | --- | ------------------------------- | --- | ------------ | --- | ------------ | --- | ------ |
|     | $`\displaystyle\mathcal{L}(F)-\min_{\textup{rank}(Z)=k}\mathcal{L}(Z)`$ | $`\displaystyle= |     | FF^{\top}-PAP |     | \_{F}^{2}+  |     | PAP-A        |     | \_{F}^{2}-( |     | A          |     | \_{F}^{2}-                      |     | \Lambda\_{k} |     | \_{F}^{2})`$ |     | (B.91) |
|     |                                                                         | $`\displaystyle= |     | FF^{\top}-PAP |     | \_{F}^{2}+( |     | \Lambda\_{k} |     | \_{F}^{2}+  |     | PAP        |     | \_{F}^{2}-2\mathrm{tr}(PAPA))`$ |     | (B.92)       |
|     |                                                                         | $`\displaystyle= |     | FF^{\top}-PAP |     | \_{F}^{2}+( |     | \Lambda\_{k} |     | \_{F}^{2}-  |     | Q^{\top}AQ |     | \_{F}^{2})`$                    |     | (B.93)       |

Where in
[Equation B.93](#A2.E93 "In Proof. ‣ B.1.4 Matrix Factorization Lemmas ‣ B.1 Preliminary Lemmas ‣ Appendix B Theorems about Diffusion Similarity and Contrastive Learning ‣ A Theoretical Framework for Self-Play Theorem Proving Algorithms"),
we used that
$`||Q^{\top}AQ||_{F}^{2}=||PAP||_{F}^{2}=\mathrm{tr}(PAPA)`$.

Because
$`\mathcal{L}(F)-\min_{\textup{rank}(Z)=k}\mathcal{L}(Z)\leq\epsilon`$
by assumption, then by
[Equation B.93](#A2.E93 "In Proof. ‣ B.1.4 Matrix Factorization Lemmas ‣ B.1 Preliminary Lemmas ‣ Appendix B Theorems about Diffusion Similarity and Contrastive Learning ‣ A Theoretical Framework for Self-Play Theorem Proving Algorithms"),
to show that $`||FF^{\top}-PAP||_{F}^{2}\leq\epsilon`$, it suffices to
show that $`||\Lambda_{k}||_{F}^{2}-||Q^{\top}AQ||_{F}^{2}\geq 0`$.
Towards this, let $`Q_{\perp}`$ complete $`Q`$ to an orthonormal basis,
so that $`I=QQ^{\top}+Q_{\perp}Q_{\perp}^{\top}`$. Then

|     |                                              |                                                                             |     |            |
| --- | -------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --- | ---------- | --- | ---------- | --- | ------------------- | --- | ------------- | --- | ---------- | --- | ----------- | --- | ------ |
|     | $`\displaystyle Q^{\top}A^{2}Q`$             | $`\displaystyle=Q^{\top}A(I)AQ`$                                            |     | (B.94)     |
|     |                                              | $`\displaystyle=Q^{\top}AQQ^{\top}AQ+Q^{\top}AQ_{\perp}Q_{\perp}^{\top}AQ`$ |     | (B.95)     |
|     | $`\displaystyle\mathrm{tr}(Q^{\top}A^{2}Q)`$ | $`\displaystyle=                                                            |     | Q^{\top}AQ |     | \_{F}^{2}+ |     | Q\_{\perp}^{\top}AQ |     | \_{F}^{2}\geq |     | Q^{\top}AQ |     | \_{F}^{2}`$ |     | (B.96) |

On the other hand, since $`P=QQ^{\top}`$ has rank $`k`$ with
$`Q^{\top}Q=I_{k}`$, by
[Lemma B.9](#A2.Thmtheorem9 "Lemma B.9. ‣ B.1.4 Matrix Factorization Lemmas ‣ B.1 Preliminary Lemmas ‣ Appendix B Theorems about Diffusion Similarity and Contrastive Learning ‣ A Theoretical Framework for Self-Play Theorem Proving Algorithms"),

|     |                                                                                                                                   |     |              |
| --- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --- | ------------ | --- | ----------- | --- | ------ |
|     | $`\displaystyle\mathrm{tr}(A^{2}P)=\mathrm{tr}(Q^{\top}A^{2}Q)\leq\sum*{i=1}^{k}\lambda*{i}(A^{2})=\sum*{i=1}^{k}\lambda*{i}^{2}= |     | \Lambda\_{k} |     | \_{F}^{2}`$ |     | (B.97) |

Combining
[Equation B.97](#A2.E97 "In Proof. ‣ B.1.4 Matrix Factorization Lemmas ‣ B.1 Preliminary Lemmas ‣ Appendix B Theorems about Diffusion Similarity and Contrastive Learning ‣ A Theoretical Framework for Self-Play Theorem Proving Algorithms")
with
[Equation B.96](#A2.E96 "In Proof. ‣ B.1.4 Matrix Factorization Lemmas ‣ B.1 Preliminary Lemmas ‣ Appendix B Theorems about Diffusion Similarity and Contrastive Learning ‣ A Theoretical Framework for Self-Play Theorem Proving Algorithms")
gives $`||Q^{\top}AQ||_{F}^{2}\leq||\Lambda_{k}||_{F}^{2}`$. By
[Equation B.93](#A2.E93 "In Proof. ‣ B.1.4 Matrix Factorization Lemmas ‣ B.1 Preliminary Lemmas ‣ Appendix B Theorems about Diffusion Similarity and Contrastive Learning ‣ A Theoretical Framework for Self-Play Theorem Proving Algorithms"),
and the fact that
$`\mathcal{L}(F)-\min_{\textup{rank}(Z)=k}\mathcal{L}(Z)\leq\epsilon`$,
we conclude that

|     |                 |     |               |
| --- | --------------- | --- | ------------- | --- | ----------------------- | --- | ------ |
|     | $`\displaystyle |     | FF^{\top}-PAP |     | \_{F}^{2}\leq\epsilon`$ |     | (B.98) |

which upper bounds the first term in our decomposition,
[Equation B.87](#A2.E87 "In Proof. ‣ B.1.4 Matrix Factorization Lemmas ‣ B.1 Preliminary Lemmas ‣ Appendix B Theorems about Diffusion Similarity and Contrastive Learning ‣ A Theoretical Framework for Self-Play Theorem Proving Algorithms").

Bounding $`||PAP-A_{k}||_{F}`$.

With $`P_{k}:=U_{k}U_{k}^{\top}`$ denoting the projector onto the
top-$`k`$ eigenspace of $`A`$, we will first argue that projectors $`P`$
and $`P_{k}`$ are close in Frobenius norm. We have

|     |                                                              |                               |     |              |
| --- | ------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------- | --- | ------------ | --- | ------------------------------- | --- | ---------- | --- | ----------- | --- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
|     | $`\displaystyle\mathrm{tr}(A^{2}P_{k})-\mathrm{tr}(A^{2}P)`$ | $`\displaystyle=              |     | \Lambda\_{k} |     | \_{F}^{2}-\mathrm{tr}(A^{2}P)`$ |     | (B.99)     |
|     |                                                              | $`\displaystyle\leq           |     | \Lambda\_{k} |     | \_{F}^{2}-                      |     | Q^{\top}AQ |     | \_{F}^{2}`$ |     | (By [Equation B.96](#A2.E96 "In Proof. ‣ B.1.4 Matrix Factorization Lemmas ‣ B.1 Preliminary Lemmas ‣ Appendix B Theorems about Diffusion Similarity and Contrastive Learning ‣ A Theoretical Framework for Self-Play Theorem Proving Algorithms") and $`P=QQ^{\top}`$) |
|     |                                                              | $`\displaystyle\leq\epsilon`$ |     | (B.100)      |

Where the last inequality is by
[Equation B.93](#A2.E93 "In Proof. ‣ B.1.4 Matrix Factorization Lemmas ‣ B.1 Preliminary Lemmas ‣ Appendix B Theorems about Diffusion Similarity and Contrastive Learning ‣ A Theoretical Framework for Self-Play Theorem Proving Algorithms"),
the non-negativity of $`||FF^{\top}-PAP||_{F}^{2}`$, and the fact that
$`\mathcal{L}(F)-\min_{\textup{rank}(Z)=k}\mathcal{L}(Z)\leq\epsilon`$.

The squared eigengap $`\lambda_{k}^{2}-\lambda_{k+1}^{2}>0`$ is positive
by assumption. Since
$`\langle A^{2},P_{k}-P\rangle=\mathrm{tr}(A^{2}P_{k})-\mathrm{tr}(A^{2}P)\leq\epsilon`$,
[Lemma B.10](#A2.Thmtheorem10 "Lemma B.10. ‣ B.1.4 Matrix Factorization Lemmas ‣ B.1 Preliminary Lemmas ‣ Appendix B Theorems about Diffusion Similarity and Contrastive Learning ‣ A Theoretical Framework for Self-Play Theorem Proving Algorithms")
([Equation B.73](#A2.E73 "In Lemma B.10. ‣ B.1.4 Matrix Factorization Lemmas ‣ B.1 Preliminary Lemmas ‣ Appendix B Theorems about Diffusion Similarity and Contrastive Learning ‣ A Theoretical Framework for Self-Play Theorem Proving Algorithms"))
implies that

|     |     |     |     |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
|     |

````math
||P_{k}-P||_{F}^{2}\leq\frac{2\epsilon}{\lambda_{k}^{2}-\lambda_{k+1}^{2}}
``` |  | (B.101) |

Write $`\Delta:=P-P_{k}`$. Note that $`A_{k}=P_{k}AP_{k}`$. We have

|  |  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|----|
|  | $`\displaystyle PAP-P_{k}AP_{k}`$ | $`\displaystyle=P_{k}A\Delta+\Delta AP_{k}+\Delta A\Delta`$ |  | (B.102) |
|  | $`\displaystyle||PAP-P_{k}AP_{k}||_{F}`$ | $`\displaystyle\leq 2||A||_{2}\,||P_{k}||_{2}\,||\Delta||_{F}+||A||_{2}\,||\Delta||_{2}\,||\Delta||_{F}`$ |  | (B.103) |
|  |  | $`\displaystyle\leq 4||A||_{2}||\Delta||_{F}`$ |  | (Since $`||P_{k}||_{2}=1`$ and $`||\Delta||_{2}\leq||P||_{2}+||P_{k}||_{2}=2`$ ) |

With
$`||\Delta||_{F}=||P-P_{k}||_{F}\leq\sqrt{\frac{2\epsilon}{\lambda_{k}^{2}-\lambda_{k+1}^{2}}}`$
from
([B.101](#A2.E101 "Equation B.101 ‣ Proof. ‣ B.1.4 Matrix Factorization Lemmas ‣ B.1 Preliminary Lemmas ‣ Appendix B Theorems about Diffusion Similarity and Contrastive Learning ‣ A Theoretical Framework for Self-Play Theorem Proving Algorithms")),
we have

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  | $`\displaystyle||PAP-A_{k}||_{F}=||PAP-P_{k}AP_{k}||_{F}\leq 4||A||_{2}\sqrt{\frac{2\epsilon}{\lambda_{k}^{2}-\lambda_{k+1}^{2}}}`$ |  | (B.104) |

Combining the Bounds.

Plugging in
[Equation B.98](#A2.E98 "In Proof. ‣ B.1.4 Matrix Factorization Lemmas ‣ B.1 Preliminary Lemmas ‣ Appendix B Theorems about Diffusion Similarity and Contrastive Learning ‣ A Theoretical Framework for Self-Play Theorem Proving Algorithms")
and
[Equation B.104](#A2.E104 "In Proof. ‣ B.1.4 Matrix Factorization Lemmas ‣ B.1 Preliminary Lemmas ‣ Appendix B Theorems about Diffusion Similarity and Contrastive Learning ‣ A Theoretical Framework for Self-Play Theorem Proving Algorithms")
into
[Equation B.87](#A2.E87 "In Proof. ‣ B.1.4 Matrix Factorization Lemmas ‣ B.1 Preliminary Lemmas ‣ Appendix B Theorems about Diffusion Similarity and Contrastive Learning ‣ A Theoretical Framework for Self-Play Theorem Proving Algorithms"),

|  |  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|----|
|  | $`\displaystyle||FF^{\top}-A_{k}||_{F}`$ | $`\displaystyle\leq||FF^{\top}-PAP||_{F}+||PAP-A_{k}||_{F}`$ |  | (B.105) |
|  |  | $`\displaystyle\leq\sqrt{\epsilon}+4||A||_{2}\sqrt{\frac{2\epsilon}{\lambda_{k}^{2}-\lambda_{k+1}^{2}}}`$ |  | (B.106) |
|  |  | $`\displaystyle=\Big(1+4||A||_{2}\sqrt{\frac{2}{\lambda_{k}^{2}-\lambda_{k+1}^{2}}}\Big)\sqrt{\epsilon}`$ |  | (B.107) |

Finally, noting that any global minimizer
$`F_{0}\in\arg\min_{\textup{rank}(Z)=k}\mathcal{L}(Z)`$ satisfies that
$`F_{0}F_{0}^{\top}=A_{k}`$, we can view $`||FF^{\top}-A_{k}||_{F}`$ as
the difference between the gram matrices of $`F`$ and a global minimizer
$`F_{0}`$.
[Lemma B.8](#A2.Thmtheorem8 "Lemma B.8. ‣ B.1.4 Matrix Factorization Lemmas ‣ B.1 Preliminary Lemmas ‣ Appendix B Theorems about Diffusion Similarity and Contrastive Learning ‣ A Theoretical Framework for Self-Play Theorem Proving Algorithms")
enables us to convert an upper bound on the Gram error
$`||FF^{\top}-A_{k}||_{F}`$ to factor error, between $`F`$ and the
closest global minimizer to it in Frobenius norm (specified by a
$`(k\times k)`$ orthogonal matrix). Let
$`F_{0}:=U_{k}\Lambda_{k}^{1/2}\in S`$ so that
$`F_{0}F_{0}^{\top}=A_{k}`$ and $`(\sigma_{k}(F_{0}))^{2}=\lambda_{k}`$.
Apply
[Lemma B.8](#A2.Thmtheorem8 "Lemma B.8. ‣ B.1.4 Matrix Factorization Lemmas ‣ B.1 Preliminary Lemmas ‣ Appendix B Theorems about Diffusion Similarity and Contrastive Learning ‣ A Theoretical Framework for Self-Play Theorem Proving Algorithms")
with $`U=F`$ and $`X=F_{0}`$, and then combine the result with
$`(\sigma_{k}(F_{0}))^{2}=\lambda_{k}`$ and
[Equation B.107](#A2.E107 "In Proof. ‣ B.1.4 Matrix Factorization Lemmas ‣ B.1 Preliminary Lemmas ‣ Appendix B Theorems about Diffusion Similarity and Contrastive Learning ‣ A Theoretical Framework for Self-Play Theorem Proving Algorithms")
to obtain:

|  |  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|----|
|  | $`\displaystyle\textup{dist}(F,F_{0})^{2}`$ | $`\displaystyle:=\min_{R\in O^{k\times k}}||F-F_{0}R||_{F}^{2}`$ |  | (B.108) |
|  |  | $`\displaystyle\leq\frac{1}{2(\sqrt{2}-1)\lambda_{k}}||FF^{\top}-A_{k}||_{F}^{2}`$ |  | (B.109) |
|  |  | $`\displaystyle\leq\frac{\Big(1+4||A||_{2}\sqrt{\frac{2}{\lambda_{k}^{2}-\lambda_{k+1}^{2}}}\Big)^{2}}{2(\sqrt{2}-1)\lambda_{k}}\epsilon.`$ |  | (B.110) |

Finally, choose $`R^{*}\in O^{k\times k}`$ that attains the minimum in
$`\textup{dist}(F,F_{0})`$ and set $`F^{*}:=F_{0}R^{*}\in S`$. Then
$`||F-F^{*}||_{F}^{2}=\textup{dist}(F,F_{0})^{2}\leq\frac{\Big(1+4||A||_{2}\sqrt{\frac{2}{\lambda_{k}^{2}-\lambda_{k+1}^{2}}}\Big)^{2}}{2(\sqrt{2}-1)\lambda_{k}}\epsilon`$,
completing the proof. ∎

[Lemma B.12](#A2.Thmtheorem12 "Lemma B.12. ‣ B.1.4 Matrix Factorization Lemmas ‣ B.1 Preliminary Lemmas ‣ Appendix B Theorems about Diffusion Similarity and Contrastive Learning ‣ A Theoretical Framework for Self-Play Theorem Proving Algorithms")
is a simple Lemma that converts the guarantee from
[Lemma B.11](#A2.Thmtheorem11 "Lemma B.11 (Approximate minimizers are close to a global minimizer). ‣ B.1.4 Matrix Factorization Lemmas ‣ B.1 Preliminary Lemmas ‣ Appendix B Theorems about Diffusion Similarity and Contrastive Learning ‣ A Theoretical Framework for Self-Play Theorem Proving Algorithms")
into one about the embedding functions parameterizing matrices
$`F_{\theta}`$ and $`F_{*}`$.

###### Lemma B.12.

Let $`n\geq k`$ be natural numbers, and matrices
$`F_{\theta},F_{*}\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times k},R\in O^{k\times k}`$ to
where $`\mathrm{dist}(F_{\theta},F_{*})=||F_{\theta}-F_{*}R||_{F}`$.
Suppose $`\pi\in\Delta([n])`$,
$`h_{\theta}:[n]\to\mathbb{R}^{k},h_{\theta_{*}}:[n]\to\mathbb{R}^{k}`$
parameterize $`F_{\theta},F_{*}`$ as follows. For all $`x\in[n]`$,

|  |  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|----|
|  | $`\displaystyle F_{\theta}[x]`$ | $`\displaystyle=\sqrt{\pi(x)}h_{\theta}(x)`$ |  | (B.111) |
|  | $`\displaystyle F_{*}[x]`$ | $`\displaystyle=\sqrt{\pi(x)}h_{\theta_{*}}(x)`$ |  | (B.112) |

Then,
$`\mathrm{dist}(F_{\theta},F_{*})^{2}=\mathbb{E}_{x\sim\pi}||h_{\theta}-R\,h_{\theta_{*}}||_{2}^{2}`$.

###### Proof.

|  |  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|----|
|  | $`\displaystyle\mathrm{dist}(F_{\theta},F_{*})^{2}`$ | $`\displaystyle=||F_{\theta}-F_{*}R||_{F}^{2}`$ |  | (B.113) |
|  |  | $`\displaystyle=\sum_{x\in[n]}\pi(x)||h_{\theta}-R\,h_{\theta_{*}}||_{2}^{2}`$ |  | (B.114) |
|  |  | $`\displaystyle=\mathbb{E}_{x\sim\pi}||h_{\theta}-R\,h_{\theta_{*}}||_{2}^{2}`$ |  | (B.115) |

∎

#### B.1.5 Learning Contrastive Embeddings on Local Subgraphs

In addition, we would like the embeddings to be learned locally, not for
the entire graph simultaneously. For a theorem graph $`G=(V,E)`$, define
the following notion of a subgraph of $`G`$ supported on the
$`T`$-neighborhood of a node $`x\in V`$. In the following, we will
denote $`(C,P,w):=(C_{w},P_{w},w)`$ as a reversible conjecturer
satisfying
[Definition 4.1](#S4.Thmtheorem1 "Definition 4.1. ‣ Conjecturer. ‣ 4.2 Random-Walk Conjecturing Algorithm ‣ 4 Framework and Random-Exploration Baseline ‣ A Theoretical Framework for Self-Play Theorem Proving Algorithms"),
to simplify notation.

See
[5.9](#S5.Thmtheorem9 "Definition 5.9 (Local Subgraph). ‣ 5.3 Computing Diffusion Similarity via Contrastive Learning ‣ 5 Diversity Measure and an Improved Conjecturing Algorithm ‣ A Theoretical Framework for Self-Play Theorem Proving Algorithms")

On a $`T=\tau+1`$ local subgraph centered at $`x\in V`$, the
$`\tau`$-step random walk distribution of $`x`$ and any neighbor
$`y\in N(x)`$ is the same as that on the entire graph.

###### Lemma B.13.

Let $`G=(V,E)`$ be a connected, undirected graph with reversible,
nearest-neighbor-type Markov chain $`(V,P)`$. Let $`T=\tau+1`$. Let
$`P_{x,T}`$ be the restriction of $`P`$ to $`G_{x,T}`$. For any
$`x\in V`$ and any $`y\in N(x)`$, we have
$`p^{\tau}_{G_{x,T}}(x)=p^{\tau}(x)`$ and
$`p^{\tau}_{G_{x,T}}(y)=p^{\tau}(y)`$, where $`p^{\tau}(x),p^{\tau}(y)`$
is the usual scale-$`\tau`$ diffusion embeddings defined in
[Definition 5.4](#S5.Thmtheorem4 "Definition 5.4. ‣ 5.2 Improved Conjecturing Algorithm ‣ 5 Diversity Measure and an Improved Conjecturing Algorithm ‣ A Theoretical Framework for Self-Play Theorem Proving Algorithms").

###### Proof.

Since $`G_{x,\tau+1}`$ is restricted to $`B(x,\tau+1)`$, then
$`G_{x,\tau+1}`$ and $`G`$ look identical to a nearest-neighbor-type
random walk starting at $`x`$ or any $`y\in N(x)`$ of length at most
$`\tau`$. ∎

[Lemma B.13](#A2.Thmtheorem13 "Lemma B.13. ‣ B.1.5 Learning Contrastive Embeddings on Local Subgraphs ‣ B.1 Preliminary Lemmas ‣ Appendix B Theorems about Diffusion Similarity and Contrastive Learning ‣ A Theoretical Framework for Self-Play Theorem Proving Algorithms")
shows the scale-$`\tau`$ diffusion embedding can be computed locally, in
a $`(\tau+1)`$ neighborhood around the queried node. In addition, for
any reversible Markov chain $`(V,P)`$ on the entire graph $`G`$ with
stationary measure $`\pi`$, for any $`x\in V`$ and $`T\in\mathbb{N}`$,
the stationary measure $`\pi_{x,T}`$ is equal to $`\pi`$ restricted to
$`B(x,T)`$, up to a multiplicative constant, by the self-loop
construction of $`G_{x,T}`$. Thus, the diffusion similarity and distance
computed locally differs from that computed globally by a multiplicative
constant, which means the locally-computed diffusion similarity is
sufficient for solving the optimization problem in
[Equation 5.3](#S5.E3 "In 5.2 Improved Conjecturing Algorithm ‣ 5 Diversity Measure and an Improved Conjecturing Algorithm ‣ A Theoretical Framework for Self-Play Theorem Proving Algorithms").

To learn the spectral diffusion embedding for reversible Markov chain
$`(V,P)`$, of conjecturer $`(C,P,w)`$ in a local $`T`$-neighborhood
around a node $`x\in V`$ via
[Algorithm 7](#alg7 "In B.1.1 Setup ‣ B.1 Preliminary Lemmas ‣ Appendix B Theorems about Diffusion Similarity and Contrastive Learning ‣ A Theoretical Framework for Self-Play Theorem Proving Algorithms"),
one will require access to the following oracles, defined in
[Definition 5.9](#S5.Thmtheorem9 "Definition 5.9 (Local Subgraph). ‣ 5.3 Computing Diffusion Similarity via Contrastive Learning ‣ 5 Diversity Measure and an Improved Conjecturing Algorithm ‣ A Theoretical Framework for Self-Play Theorem Proving Algorithms").

1.  1.
    The push-forward map $`C_{x,T}:B(x,T)\to\Delta(B(x,T))`$ of the
    restricted Markov chain $`(V_{x,T},P_{x,T})`$, where
    $`\forall y\in B(x,T)`$, $`C_{x,T}(y)=P_{x,T}[y]\in\Delta(B(x,T))`$,
2.  2.
    i.i.d. sample access to $`\pi_{x,T}\in\Delta(B(x,T))`$.

For $`(V_{x,T},P_{x,T})`$, it suffices to have access to the original
conjecturer $`(C,P,w):=(C_{w},P_{w},w)`$ on $`G`$ and the neighbor
oracle $`N_{G_{x,T}}:V\to 2^{V}`$ of the local graph $`G_{x,T}`$
supported on $`B(x,T)`$. This is because for any $`y\in B(x,T)`$, to
sample $`z\sim C_{x,T}(y)`$, one can first sample
$`z^{\prime}\sim C(y)`$. Then, if $`z^{\prime}\in N_{G_{x,T}}(y)`$, set
$`z=z^{\prime}`$. Else, set $`z=y`$. $`z`$ will be a sample from
$`C_{x,T}(y)`$ with the correct distribution.

[Algorithm 8](#alg8 "In B.1.5 Learning Contrastive Embeddings on Local Subgraphs ‣ B.1 Preliminary Lemmas ‣ Appendix B Theorems about Diffusion Similarity and Contrastive Learning ‣ A Theoretical Framework for Self-Play Theorem Proving Algorithms")
describes how to compute $`N_{G_{x,T}}:V\to 2^{V}`$ and $`\pi_{x,T}`$.
It involves first performing a $`T`$-step BFS starting from node $`x`$.
Once the set of all theorems in the $`T`$-neighborhood of $`x`$ is
collected, it is straightforward to create an oracle for
$`N_{G_{x,T}}`$. Regarding the sampler for $`\pi_{x,T}`$, because
$`\forall y\in B(x,T),\pi_{x,T}(y)\propto\pi(y)\propto w(y)`$, then
$`\pi_{x,T}(y)=\frac{w(y)}{\sum_{z\in B(x,T)}w(z)}`$. It suffices to
compute the vector $`\pi_{x,T}`$ for all $`y\in B(x,T)`$.

1: $`T\in\mathbb{N}`$, source theorem $`x\in V`$, neighbor oracle
$`N:V\to 2^{V}`$, and conjecturer $`(C,P,w):=(C_{w},P_{w},w)`$

2: Local neighbor oracle $`N_{G_{x,T}}:B(x,T)\to 2^{B(x,T)}`$ and local
stationary measure $`\pi_{x,T}\in\Delta(B(x,T))`$

3: Set $`B_{-1}\leftarrow\emptyset`$ and $`B_{0}\leftarrow\{x\}`$

4: for $`s=1,\ldots,T`$ do

5:   Set $`\partial B_{s-1}\leftarrow B_{s-1}\setminus B_{s-2}`$

6:   Set
$`B_{s}\leftarrow B_{s-1}\cup\bigcup_{v\in\partial B_{s-1}}N(v).`$

7: Set $`S\leftarrow B_{T}`$

8:

9: Define $`N_{G_{x,T}}`$ by the following subroutine:

10:   Local Neighbor Oracle $`N_{G_{x,T}}`$:

11:    Input: $`y\in S`$

12:    Query $`N(y)`$

13:    Set $`m(y)\leftarrow|N(y)\cap S|`$

14:    return $`N(y)\cap S`$ together with $`\deg(y)-m(y)`$ copies of
$`y`$   

15: Set

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\pi_{x,T}(y)\leftarrow\frac{w(y)}{\sum_{z\in S}w(z)}\qquad\text{for all }y\in S.
``` |  |

16: return $`N_{G_{x,T}}`$ and $`\pi_{x,T}`$
````
